{"data":{"feed":{"__typename":"Feed","updated":"2026-07-19T02:30:47.149104Z","pets":[{"id":"251907","name":"Ace Of Hearts","age":"3 Years","type":"Dog","species":"Dog","link":"https://nycacc.app/browse/251907","gender":"Male","summaryHtml":"My foster writes: Meet your new cuddle buddy! This sweet, affectionate boy loves being close to his people and is known for giving actual hugs-he'll wrap his front legs around you and rest his head while soaking up the attention. He gets so excited for mealtime that he jumps and spins, loves car rides and playing in the sprinklers, and will happily curl up next to you on the couch for movie night. He even watches TV and tries to follow the ball during basketball games! With his funny personality and loving nature, he's sure to bring plenty of smiles and snuggles to his future home.

Meet Ace of Hearts!
Ace of Hearts was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him. He previously lived with adults, and is described as a highly social, wiggly, and affectionate dog who loves interacting with people. He comes over readily for attention, leans into touch, and enjoys playtime, often offering play bows and engaging happily with toys.

My Ideal Home
Ace would do best in a calm, patient home that can support him as he settles in and builds confidence. He can be anxious at times and may pace or have trouble settling, especially in new environments, so a consistent routine and a quiet space will help him feel more secure.

Good with Other Pets?
Ace has shown neutral behavior around dogs at the shelter, but he is not a match for homes with cats due to lunging toward them on walks. Continued positive reinforcement training and management will be important when navigating environments with other animals.

Good with Kids?
A home without young children under 5 is recommended due to his sensitivity to handling and tendency to become fearful when startled.

Things to Know
Ace is a sweet and people-oriented dog who enjoys affection and play, but he can be sensitive to loud noises, sudden movements, and handling around his paws. He may also feel anxious when left alone. He responds best to gentle, choice-based interactions and should never be forced into situations that make him uncomfortable. With time, structure, and positive reinforcement, he has great potential to feel more confident and settled in a home.

Fun Fact
Ace of Hearts lives up to his name, he is all heart when it comes to his people and loves being right by your side soaking up attention. They enjoy play wrestling and relaxing together for very funny and entertaining viewing. Alex can be a bit more independent and likes to go on his own mini adventures. His true joys are during playtime as he loves to show off his jumps and acrobatic skills. Extra high jumps if he gets the chance to play on the couch or bed! Outside of play, Alex likes his peace and quiet and curling up for favorite naps. He gives you your space during the day to get work done, but might come by and lie down near your feet just to do a quick check-in. Alex is not necessarily one for cuddles and brushes, instead he bonds with you through fun and games. He should be going to a home that is a bit more quiet as both him and Marley prefer slow introductions to new people and surroundings. Once he does however, Alex makes for a great cat buddy who is always down for some fun.

Alex is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. They are apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, they appreciate attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people, we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

I came in with multiple cats and am currently housed with my sibling, Marley (225640) who I am bonded with! (as seen in photo)

A volunteer writes: Visiting with Alex and Marley (225640) makes me feel like I've walked into a play. Except both of these adorable cats seem to patiently and adorably look to us for their entertainment. With one paw delicately perched on the ledge of his bed, Alex waited for me to introduce myself before presenting his neck for some scritches. Marley, meanwhile, prefers her perch to being downstairs when there are guests but she really, really loves pets. The circumstances need to be just right (i.e., calm and quiet) and when they are, she very sweetly leans in. They loved watching me try to play with them and every so often, Alex would stretch a paw up for the pipe cleaner feather. Alex and Marley came to us from a home with many other cats. Settling into any new environment comes with challenges and we're grateful that Alex and Marley have found so much comfort in each other. Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconazole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!

Hi, my name is Allie and the shelter has been a little overwhelming for me. I came from a home with many cats, who I've gotten along with well. Because I've lived in this home my entire life and have only been around one person, I have little experience with people and am hesitant of new experiences. I would enjoy living in a quiet home, preferably one with lots of vertical space so I have a place to perch and observe the room. I would also appreciate having experienced, patient adopter(s) who are willing to take things slow with me. I would benefit from socialization, using rewards whenever I make a small positive step like making eye contact, allowing petting, or sniffing your hand. I'd prefer to take things at my own pace and would appreciate some good old fashion TLC. If you can open your heart to adopt a cat like me, I'll hopefully have the confidence to come around to my new people, like you!

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! Almond is a 3-year-old large mixed breed who was found as a stray in the Bronx and has since spent time in a foster home. This affectionate and playful girl is eager to find her forever home where she can be loved and cherished. My Ideal Home Almond would thrive in a home that provides both structure and activity. She has an energetic personality and would benefit from regular exercise, training, and positive reinforcement. She is best suited for an adult-only home or a home with older children who can respect her space and help reinforce good manners. Good with Kids? Almond would do best in a home without young children due to her excitable nature and tendency to jump up in a social manner. Older kids who understand dog behavior may be a better fit. Good with Other Dogs? Almond has had mixed reactions to other dogs-sometimes greeting them with a loose, wiggly body and other times barking and jumping at the fence. She would need slow, positive introductions if placed in a home with another dog. Good with Cats? Unknown-she has not been tested with cats. Leash Manners Almond is strong on the leash and can be reactive toward dogs and small animals while walking. A front-clip harness and reward-based training will help manage this behavior. Overall Health She has no ongoing medical concerns, though she is slightly overweight and would benefit from a balanced diet and exercise. Behavior Determination Level 3 (Experienced Adopters Recommended) - Almond is a sweet and affectionate dog who loves attention but needs continued training for her manners, anxiety, and leash reactivity. She thrives with positive reinforcement and would do best in a structured environment. What Her Friends Say 💬 "Almond is very sweet! She loves to play, licks a lot as a show of love, and enjoys belly rubs. She listens to commands like sit, wait, and go." -Her Foster 💬 "She was the perfect Borough Break buddy-affectionate, playful, and well-behaved on leash. She made our day and will make someone very happy!" -Volunteer If you're looking for a fun-loving, affectionate dog who will bring energy and joy into your life, Almond could be the perfect match for you! Whether you're out for a stroll or just relaxing at home, Almond is always by your side, ready to share her love and bring joy to your life. What my friends at ACC say about me:

I'm an independent kitty who likes to do my own thing.

I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.

I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.

I am looking for a home with a patient person.

I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

A volunteer writes: Andy misses the life he had before his elderly owner could no longer take care of him--his own space in the living room, a soft carpet to nap on, and the security of knowing he belonged to someone. Now he's at the Care Center, where he's doing his best to show what a good boy he is. Shy at first, Andy is a fan of slow blinks and gentle pets on his head. Toys don't interest him as much as treats do; he relaxes when humans talk to him. This chunky monkey seems to prefer an easygoing life of laying around and being loved, and we just know there's a pet parent or family out there who can make that happen for this sweet, subdued guy. Meet Andy at the Manhattan Care Center today!

I have lived with cats at ACC and I'm doing well with them in the Free Roaming Room, so I would likely do well in a multi-cat home.

I prioritize my well-being and channel my energy into my corrugated scratch board. I'm a bit on the shy side, but don't let that fool you-once I feel a connection, I'll strut over to your feet and give you a chirp of approval. I love being pampered with Temptations and Delectable treats, served straight from your hand. When I'm not busy fending off the neighborhood ladies sneaking past my window, I retreat to my cozy cardboard villa to recharge. It's my personal hideaway, but don't worry-I'll come to you when I'm ready. Secure your cabinets! I consider myself an explorer at heart and enjoy uncovering closed spaces. I'm currently employed as a personal towel warmer, though I must admit, I'm often caught napping on the job. I'm searching for someone who will patiently help me blossom and build my confidence. Apollo is a playful pup looking for a family ready to join him on his next adventure. After being surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him, Apollo is hoping to find a forever home where he can keep learning, playing, and soaking up all the love. This energetic guy has a big personality and is ready to become someone's out-of-this-world companion!

My Ideal Home
Apollo would thrive with an active family who can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. He is a smart pup who enjoys engaging with his people and will benefit from continued practice with polite greetings and impulse control. With the right guidance, Apollo is ready to rocket into his best life!

Good with Other Pets?
Apollo's previous family shared that he can bark and growl at dogs and small animals on walks as a way of trying to initiate play. He would benefit from continued leash training and positive reinforcement to help him learn calmer ways to interact with the world around him. Slow introductions would be recommended when meeting new furry friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Apollo's fearful behaviors and leash reactivity, an adult-only home is recommended at this time. He would do best with people who can help him build confidence while continuing to practice his manners.

Things to Know
Apollo is an energetic and playful dog who loves staying busy! He enjoys attention from his people and is comfortable with handling, including having his paws and collar touched. His previous family shared that he enjoys using wee-wee pads indoors and can be a bit of a curious explorer, so providing appropriate chew toys and enrichment will help keep his busy brain and playful paws occupied. Apollo is ready to find a family who will help him shine! My foster writes: Burrata and Basil are two young sister cats who bring a calm, gentle presence to the home. Since arriving, we've learned that they love observing everything around them. They have the sweetest, most curious little expressions, sometimes it genuinely feels like they're quietly "commenting" on whatever we're doing, and it always makes us smile. He has enjoyed relaxed greetings, engaged in playful interactions with another dog, and has generally ignored dogs while out on walks. As always, slow introductions to resident pets are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to his fearful nature and need for a calm environment, ACC recommends an adult only home.

Things to Know

He's made wonderful progress during his time at the shelter, now walking beautifully on a loose leash, calmly passing people and dogs, and allowing gentle handling with patient, low-pressure interactions. He'll do best with an adopter who understands that confidence is built one positive experience at a time and is willing to let him come out of his shell at his own pace.

Fun Fact
Once he's out on a walk, Bearstein is a true gentleman, strolling politely on a loose leash and taking in the world one sniff at a time. Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! Meet Bell Pepper!
Bell Pepper is an 11-year-old sweetheart who came to us as an owner surrender. She has lived with adults and is described as friendly, outgoing, and playful with new people. She enjoys attention but prefers to engage on her own terms. She is the kind of dog who likes to be near her people and soak up the calm moments of the day.

Personality
Bell Pepper enjoys being part of whatever her people are doing. She loves a good cuddle session and is happiest when she can relax close to someone she trusts. She is more of a couch potato than a toy player and enjoys fuzzy blankets. She can be a little anxious at times, so she will benefit from structure and supervision in a home.

Daily Life
Bell Pepper walks nicely on leash with no pulling and does not react to people or other dogs while out. She enjoys a calm, steady routine and tends to keep to herself in new environments until she feels comfortable. Once settled, she is easygoing and enjoys simply being near her person. She is partially crate trained and can stay in a crate for up to several hours as long as it is large enough for her to move comfortably.

Training and Manners
Bell Pepper knows several cues including sit, stay, paw, and go. She is treat motivated and will happily take most foods offered to her. She is not reactive toward people on walks and handles gentle and more active handling well, standing still and tolerating contact. She may be a bit more reserved in unfamiliar situations but recovers quickly once she feels safe.

Social Behavior
Bell Pepper is generally soft and low key in new environments. She may take a moment to warm up and will approach when coaxed. She enjoys calm interaction and prefers gentle engagement over high energy play.

My Ideal Home
Bell Pepper would do best in a calm home with adults who can provide structure, routine, and gentle guidance. She would love a cozy environment where she can relax, enjoy couch time, and be included in daily life. She may benefit from continued support around her anxiety and supervision to prevent unwanted behaviors like counter surfing or getting into the garbage.

Living with Kids
She would do best in a home without young children due to her anxiety. She may be open to older, respectful teens who understand her need for space and calm interactions.

Fun Fact
Bell Pepper is a professional snuggler. Once she trusts you, she is happiest just being your quiet little shadow.

A volunteer writes: Bell Pepper 🫑 if a girl could be more my type, then I haven't met her yet. She is 11 years old, but none the wiser to that fact. Age is just a number, and Bell is the definition of young at heart. She bounds towards us, confident and happy. Jumps around for treats, trying to impress us with her sassy sit (and succeeding). She is so full of life and fun that it lifts our spirits and fills us with laughter. I joke that I'd keep her name and call her Bell when she's sweet and Pepper when she's spicy. Bello arrived at the shelter as a stray, so while his past is a mystery, we know he has a sweet and gentle side that shines through. This handsome boy is learning to trust again and has shown that he loves spending time with people once he feels comfortable. Bello enjoys affection, takes treats nicely, and has a special way of making connections with the humans around him.

My Ideal Home
Bello would do best with a patient adopter who understands that building trust takes time. He will thrive in a calm, predictable environment where he can move at his own pace and continue gaining confidence. Positive reinforcement, enrichment activities, and gentle interactions will help Bello feel safe and supported as he settles into his new life.

Good with Other Pets?
Bello's history with other animals is unknown, but he has had some interactions with other dogs while at the shelter. He has shown the ability to greet and disengage appropriately, though his comfort level can depend on the situation. Due to his body language during dog interactions, a home without dog parks is recommended, and any future dog introductions should be slow and thoughtful.

Good with Kids?
Due to Bello's handling sensitivities and moments when he has felt uncomfortable, an adult-only home is recommended at this time. Bello would do best with people who can respect his boundaries, allow him to make choices, and help him feel secure as he adjusts to his new surroundings.

Things to Know
Bello is a sensitive pup who may need extra time to feel comfortable in new situations. During his time at the shelter, he has shown signs of anxiety and can become overwhelmed, so a calm routine and patient approach will be important. Bello should be allowed to approach new experiences at his own pace and will benefit from force-free training, enrichment, and plenty of positive experiences. Once he trusts you, you may discover the sweet, affectionate dog who loves nothing more than leaning in for attention and being by your side.

Volunteer Love
A volunteer writes: I recently discovered something truly adorable about Bello: he's a hugger! During a walk, Bello politely stood by my side while I chatted with a staff member. After a few minutes, he gently placed his paws on my arms and looked up at me with the sweetest, softest expression. As I gave him some gentle pets, he leaned right in, snuggled his head into my arm, and completely melted my heart.

Volunteer Love
A volunteer writes: As I began slowly rubbing his cheeks and chin, he leaned into me with a dreamy, blissful expression. And as I gently pet along his back, he snuggled his head into the crook of my arm. Bello was more than happy to lean back in and soak up all the affection I showered on him. It's amazing how quickly Bello has warmed up and felt trustful enough to solicit attention and initiate hugs. I honestly don't think it's possible to meet Bello and not fall in love with him. He's so sweet, gentle, and affectionate; and has a way of making you feel that the very best part of his day is being with you.

Considering what sounds like a difficult past, it is incredible how quickly Bello has learned to trust and seek out affection. He is a treat-loving, gentle pup who knows "sit," takes treats nicely, and has shown polite leash manners. Bello has a way of making you feel like being with you is the highlight of his day, and he is ready to find someone who will show him just how loved he can be. Big Mama was brought in by the NYPD after being found with multiple puncture wounds, likely from another animal. Despite everything she's been through, she has remained incredibly affectionate, social, and resilient. Her bite wounds have fully healed, and she's now ready to leave shelter life behind for a loving forever home.

My Ideal Home
Big Mama would do best in a loving home that can continue supporting her recovery while giving her the stability and affection she clearly craves. She enjoys being around people and would thrive with a family that appreciates a sweet, attention seeking companion.

Good with Other Pets?
Big Mama has shown neutral behavior around other dogs in the shelter setting. Slow, thoughtful introductions are recommended as she settles into a new environment.

Good with Kids?
No young children under 5 are recommended due to some resource guarding around toys.

Things to Know
Big Mama is a soft, wiggly girl who loves attention and happily leans into affection from handlers. She walks nicely on leash, greets people warmly, and has shown a very social personality despite her difficult past. She does appear to value certain toys and may hover over them, so continued positive reinforcement training around sharing and trading items will help her succeed. Because one of her injuries was likely a bite wound, her future adopter will need to complete a little extra paperwork and continue with a few follow up vet visits this year, but she has been recovering wonderfully and her wounds are fully healed.

Fun Fact
Big Mama may have had a rough start, but her favorite thing now seems to be soaking up love and giving full body wiggles to everyone she meets. A volunteer writes: At 80 pounds, Big Mama has earned her adorable name. Found stray with 11 punctures from bites of an unknown origin, Big Mama has recovered well at the shelter. In spite of whatever happened before she arrived, her notes and interactions with staff all indicate she's an affectionate, social and resilient girl. She's also a toy loving girl, and once we give her one, it doesn't leave her side. Or more specifically her paws, as she perfectly positions and holds it to chew and squeak at us. Big Mama attempts to roll over onto her side a few times, and maybe it's her mobility or the heat, but she abandons her attempts to give us that glorious belly to rub. Because of those bites, Big Mama will need a little extra paperwork to take home, but the process isn't daunting and shouldn't deter anyone. Big Mama is ready to go home today and is available to level 2 homes - so ones with just a bit of experience. Biggs was found abandoned with three other dogs and is now looking for a fresh start with a family who will help him settle into the good life he deserves. He's social, people oriented, and has a big personality that comes out once he feels comfortable.

My Ideal Home
Biggs would do best with an adopter who can provide structure, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training to help guide his enthusiasm. He enjoys attention and engagement from people and will thrive with daily physical and mental exercise like walks, puzzle toys, and interactive play. A home that can continue working on leash manners and impulse control will help him really shine.

Good with Other Pets?
Biggs has shown some interest in other dogs at the care center, but also tends to pull strongly toward smaller dogs on leash. His history with other animals is unknown, so slow, controlled introductions would be important if living with another pet.

Good with Kids?
Due to potential resource guarding tendencies and his strength and enthusiasm, Biggs is recommended for a home without young children at this time.

Things to Know
Biggs is a social and affectionate boy who enjoys being around people and seeks out attention readily. He can be strong on leash and may redirect his energy toward other dogs or exciting stimuli, so he'll do best with continued training and management. He has shown possible interest in guarding valued items, so ongoing trade up games and positive reinforcement around handling and resources will be important. With consistency and structure, Biggs has all the makings of a loyal, fun, and engaging companion.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes: Biggs is giving main character energy from the moment you meet him. He's a social, handsome guy who leans in for attention and happily accepts treats like he's starring in his own feel good rom com. Out in the yard, he's engaged and people focused, soaking up interaction and showing off his affectionate side. You might say he's looking for someone to be his "Mr. Biggs," the steady presence who matches his charm, guides his enthusiasm, and takes him on all the best adventures the city has to offer. With the right home, this boy is ready for his happily ever after.

Fun Fact
Biggs is the kind of dog who believes every walk should come with a little drama, a lot of heart, and maybe a snack break on a park bench. Bilbo Waggins was found neglected in an apartment and has shown himself to be a sweet, goofy, and social young dog who is eager for connection. Despite his difficult start, he is affectionate, people oriented, and enjoys engaging with handlers once he feels comfortable.

My Ideal Home
Bilbo Waggins would do best in a patient, structured home that can help him build confidence at his own pace. He benefits from calm environments, consistent routines, and positive reinforcement training to support his confidence and leash skills.

Good with Other Pets?
Bilbo Waggins has shown friendly and social behavior with other dogs during controlled introductions, though he can become fearful when passing barking dogs and should have gradual, supported exposure.

Good with Kids?
Due to fearfulness and sensitivity in new environments, Bilbo Waggins is recommended for a home without children under 13.

Things to Know
Bilbo Waggins is a social and affectionate dog who enjoys attention, toys, and being close to people. He can show mild leash biting when excited or overstimulated and may become anxious in stressful environments, especially around loud or barking dogs. He has shown some sensitivity around handling his neck area and benefits from gentle, gradual handling and positive associations. With structure, patience, and reassurance, he continues to show his loving, goofy personality and strong desire to bond with people.

Volunteer Note
A volunteer writes: Bilbo was just a delight the second we met him. He is a big, goofy guy, weighing in at 66 pounds. Visually, he's very much a meathead, a jock. But inside he is just a lover boy waiting for the right person to come his way. A hopeless romantic, Bilbo would definitely be the type of guy to bring you flowers on the first date, or at least a stuffed flower toy. His love language is between gift giving and physical touch, because he is known to be a major lap dog too! Bilbo was reported to be left in a vacant apartment with other dogs. He is about 2 years old. He is super soft, social and playful. Walking past kennels, Bilbo can be a little scared, but when greeting a dog outside he displayed loose body language with wagging tail.

Fun Fact
Bilbo Waggins may look like a big goofy jock, but he is really a soft-hearted romantic who just wants to be someone's loyal best friend. Years","type":"Dog","species":"Dog","link":"https://nycacc.app/browse/257759","gender":"Male","summaryHtml":"Meet Blanko!
Blanko came to the shelter when his owner could no longer care for him and is looking for a fresh start with an experienced adopter. This energetic, playful boy loves spending time with people and is always ready for fun. He has a big personality and an even bigger heart, and with the right guidance, he's ready to become an incredible companion.

My Ideal Home
Blanko would thrive with an active, adult only household that can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. Puzzle toys, long walks, training sessions, and interactive games will help keep both his body and mind engaged. A predictable routine and patient guidance will help him build confidence and practice calm behaviors.

Good with Other Pets?
Blanko has lived with and enjoyed spending time with familiar dogs, but he can be uncomfortable around unfamiliar dogs and has a history of conflict with other dogs. For that reason, he is looking for a home where he can be your one and only pet, and dog parks are not recommended.

Good with Kids?
Blanko is searching for an adult only home. He is an enthusiastic dog who sometimes forgets just how big he is and can become overly excited, so he'll do best with adults who can help him continue working on his manners and impulse control.

Things to Know
Blanko is an active, social dog who loves to play but is still learning how to channel his excitement appropriately. He may jump up when greeting people, pull on leash, or become overstimulated in busy environments, but he responds well to positive reinforcement and will benefit from continued training. He can also be anxious around loud noises or when left alone, so a calm, patient home will help him settle in. With structure, consistency, and lots of love, Blanko has all the ingredients to become a wonderful lifelong companion. Bluey arrived at the shelter as a stray, so while we don't know much about his past, we do know one thing for sure: this sweet boy loves making connections with people! Bluey is a social, affectionate pup who happily leans into pets and is always ready to spend time with his favorite humans. Now he's looking for a family who can help him continue learning and growing.

My Ideal Home
Bluey would thrive with an adopter who enjoys an active, playful companion and is excited to continue working on his manners. He is a smart and eager-to-learn pup who will benefit from positive reinforcement training, daily exercise, and enrichment activities that help him channel his enthusiasm in fun ways. With a little guidance, Bluey is ready to become your best adventure buddy.

Good with Other Pets?
Bluey's history with other animals is unknown, but he has shown interest in meeting other dogs while at the shelter. He has had some appropriate greetings with other dogs, though he can become tense when seeing dogs while on leash. Slow introductions and continued positive reinforcement training will help him feel comfortable and successful around canine friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Bluey's energetic play style and leash-related behaviors, an adult-only home is recommended at this time. He would do best with people who can help him practice polite greetings and build confidence through training.

Things to Know
Bluey is a happy, people-loving pup who can get a little excited when greeting his favorite humans. He may jump up when seeking attention and has been known to grab the leash when overstimulated, so continued practice with calm walking and impulse control will help him succeed. Bluey loves affection, enjoys learning, and is ready to find someone who will give him the structure, patience, and love he needs to shine. Bowie is a sweet, thoughtful boy who was found as a stray and is still learning to feel comfortable in new situations. He is very treat-motivated and shines brightest when he feels safe and understands what is being asked of him. Bowie is part of our Shelter Scholar program, where he is working on resource guarding and building confidence through positive reinforcement and structured support. He is just waiting for the right home to help him hit all the right notes.

Personality
Bowie is affectionate and people-oriented, but can be cautious in unfamiliar environments. Once he warms up, he enjoys treats, gentle interaction, and showing off his sit and paw for snacks. He does best when he can approach at his own pace and have a calm, predictable routine.

My Ideal Home
Bowie would thrive in a quiet, adult-only home with patient adopters who can move at his pace. He will benefit from structure, consistency, and continued positive reinforcement training. A low-traffic home where he can relax and feel secure will help him do his best.

Good with Other Pets?
Bowie has shown discomfort around other dogs in some introductions and may become overwhelmed in close or high-energy interactions. He also prefers not to share valued items like food, toys, or bedding. At this time, he may do best as the only pet in the home.

Good with Kids?
Bowie would do best in a home without children under 13. He is most comfortable in a calm environment where his space is respected.

Things to Know
Bowie walks nicely on leash and is generally calm in low-distraction environments. He is very food-motivated and responds well to treats and gentle guidance during training. He is actively working on resource guarding in our Shelter Scholar program and is making steady progress with support and positive reinforcement.

Fun Fact
Bowie is a clever, treat-loving boy who loves showing off his sit and paw, especially when snacks are involved. Once he feels at home, he has a soft, snuggly side that really shines. He's ready to become your new favorite record on repeat.

Brock was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him and has since shown himself to be a smart, social, and affectionate "brindle potato" with a big heart and an even bigger personality. He's a true people-lover who enjoys making friends wherever he goes and settles into routines quickly.

My Ideal Home
Brock would do best with an adopter who understands resource guarding and can manage mealtime and high-value items appropriately. He thrives with structure, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. He especially enjoys food-based activities like training games and puzzle toys, and will benefit from calm, consistent handling around valued items.

Good with Other Pets?
Brock has shown mixed but generally social interactions with other dogs in care, including loose and playful moments. His comfort level can vary, so slow, supervised introductions are recommended if living with another dog. He has shown strong reactions to cats and would likely do best without feline companions.

Good with Kids?
Due to resource guarding behaviors and mouthiness with food, Brock would do best in a home without young children.

Things to Know
Brock is a highly food-motivated, intelligent dog who learns quickly and enjoys working with his people. He can be clumsy and excitable at times, but also knows how to settle in and enjoy quiet companionship. He benefits from clear routines and positive reinforcement, especially around food and high-value items. With guidance, he is a wonderful mix of goofy energy and calm couch cuddles.

Foster Notes
My foster writes: Meet Brock, a beautiful brindle potato with a heart of gold! Brock was so sweet and trusting with us from the get go, and I believe he will easily bond with anyone who shows him love and takes good care of him. He is very smart and observant and picks up on routines quickly, knows lots of commands such as sit, stay, come, down and paw, and has a lot of potential for further training as he is VERY food motivated and lives for a tasty treat! Brock is a social butterfly and loves all people, making friends and admirers everywhere he goes. Despite being a seasoned older gentleman he retains a playful, puppy-like energy when he's excited, but he also loves being a couch potato and will happily lounge with you and lay his big head in your lap while you watch TV. Brock has brought so much love and joy into our lives as a foster, and whoever adopts him will be so lucky to have him! Brow is a gentle, sensitive boy who appreciates a soft approach and a little time to warm up. He's not pushy or demanding, more of a "take things at your pace" kind of dog. Once he feels safe, he begins to check in with his handler and engage in a quiet, steady way that shows his softer side.

Home Life
Brow will do best in an adult only home that can offer patience, structure, and a peaceful environment. He thrives with slow introductions and a predictable routine that helps him feel safe and confident over time.

He also benefits from enrichment like puzzle feeders and thoughtful activities that help keep his mind busy in a positive way.

Things to Know
Brow does best with a gentle, force-free approach and continued support around leash skills and confidence building. He's still learning that the world can be a safe and steady place, and he does best with people who are willing to go at his pace.

Fun Fact
Underneath his cautious exterior, Brow has a sweet, curious side that shines through when he feels comfortable, like a quiet little companion slowly learning to trust his world. 🐾

Caffery is a soft-hearted boy who was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him. Caffery is calm, observant, and tends to take a step back in new situations before engaging. He enjoys quiet, gentle interaction and accepts handling well when he feels safe. Once comfortable, he can relax and show a soft, easygoing side.

My Ideal Home
Caffery would thrive in a quiet, low-traffic home with a steady routine. He will do best with patient adopters who use positive reinforcement and allow him to build confidence gradually. A calm environment will help him continue to come out of his shell over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Caffery has shown a soft, friendly approach toward other dogs but can become overwhelmed if interactions are too forward or energetic. He does best with calm, respectful dogs and slow introductions. Careful matches and supervision will help set him up for success.

Good with Kids?
Caffery would do best in a home without young children under 5. He is most comfortable in calm environments where interactions are gentle and predictable.

Things to Know
Caffery is still gaining confidence on leash and may hesitate in unfamiliar settings. He benefits from slow introductions, routine, and enrichment like puzzle toys to help him stay engaged and relaxed. With consistency and patience, he continues to build trust in new experiences.

Fun Fact
Caffery has a quiet, endearing presence and a soft charm that comes out once he feels at ease. He's the kind of companion who forms a deep, steady bond with his people over time.

Casentino is the longest stay dog at Queens ACC and a truly special boy who has already come so far. He was found as a stray and arrived very overwhelmed and stressed, but with time, care, and consistency he has slowly started to show his brighter personality. His adoption fee has been sponsored, and he is more than ready for a patient home to help him continue his journey. Bushwick Bark has generously donated a goodie bag of treats and toys to get him started in his new home! Come to Queens to meet him and help him explore his gifts!

Personality
Casentino is a thoughtful, sensitive dog who does best when given time and space to feel comfortable. In the past, he struggled with stress and found it hard to focus, but now he is showing steady progress and a growing sense of confidence. He is beginning to reveal a more relaxed, affectionate side, especially with people he trusts.

When he feels safe, Casentino enjoys gentle attention and even gets wiggly with soft voices and familiar people. He knows "sit," enjoys treats, and is starting to show interest in toys, which is a big milestone for him. He still prefers affection on his own terms, but with patience he continues to open up more and more.

Out and About
Casentino walks better and more calmly than when he first arrived. He is able to stay engaged with his handler. He does not focus on other dogs on walks and generally moves through the environment without fixation, especially when supported with structure and reassurance.

He is also part of the Shelter Scholars program, where he is actively working on staying focused during walks and building confidence around distractions using positive reinforcement. He is making big progress!

Social Behavior
Casentino is learning to trust and relax in new environments. In his kennel, he now shows a soft, wiggly greeting style, often stretching and approaching with a loose body and wagging tail. br />
Home Life
Casentino will thrive in an adult only home that can offer patience, structure, and time to continue building his confidence. He has made incredible progress in a shelter environment, and there is strong potential for him to blossom even more once he is in a stable home setting.

Things to Know
Casentino is housebroken, enjoys quiet rest periods, and is continuing to grow in comfort with handling and daily routines. A volunteer describes how he has gone from highly stressed to much more settled, now able to relax, enjoy treats, and engage in simple enrichment. He will benefit greatly from continued positive reinforcement training and a patient adopter who understands sensitive dogs.

Fun Fact
Casentino is a perfect example of a dog who just needs time to shine. From a stressed stray to a pup who now stretches, wags, and leans into gentle affection, he's quietly writing his own comeback story and is ready for someone to help him finish it. 🐾

My foster writes: Don't let his appearance fool you, this guy is a sweetheart. When he isn't curled up on his bed, he loves a good game of tug of war or rolling around on his back getting pets. Casentino has been the best foster dog. He is perfectly house trained, doesn't beg for food, and has no destructive behaviors. Years","type":"Dog","species":"Dog","link":"https://nycacc.app/browse/251817","gender":"Male","summaryHtml":"Meet Casper!
Casper was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him, and now this sweet, low energy boy is looking for a soft place to land. His previous family describes him as social, affectionate, house trained, and a big fan of car rides and spending time close to his people.

My Ideal Home
Casper would do best in a calm adult-only home where he can continue healing and settle in at his own pace. He's looking for patient adopters who can give him stability, kindness, and lots of cozy downtime while he regains his confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
According to his previous owner, Casper has been friendly and outgoing with other dogs both on and off leash. At the shelter, he showed interest in greeting another dog through the gate, though interactions have remained limited while he focuses on healing.

Good with Kids?
We recommend an adult-only home for Casper at this time due to his discomfort with novel situations and handling while recovering medically.

Things to Know
Casper is currently recovering from ongoing skin issues and has been unable to complete a full handling assessment while receiving treatment. Even so, he has remained gentle with staff, takes treats softly, and continues to tolerate care and medical handling well. He can become a little timid in unfamiliar situations and may bark or growl at strangers approaching his family on walks, but overall he is described as an affectionate, easygoing companion who enjoys being near his people. Casper also loves car rides and already has great house manners.

Fun Fact
Casper may be named after a friendly ghost, but this Casper prefers cozy naps, car rides, and sticking close to his favorite humans. A volunteer writes: Casper 🥰 8 year old Casper has spent the last 2 months in the shelter, much of it in a too small kennel in an overflow room. With few breaks from his living space, it's no minor feat that he's maintained his good nature. But he patiently waits for walks, and I think hopes for some butt scratches and affection from his human companions. His skin must be itchy, and it's scabbed over when we meet. His guardian reported that he developed skin issues 2 years ago and interventions from his vet were not successful and abandoned about a year ago. Regardless, he's a little gentleman. Good with Other Pets?
Chai has shown interest in other dogs, but she can be reactive on-leash and may bark or pull towards them. My foster writes: Champ is, well, a Champion of many things. But above all - he is a champion cuddler. Charli interacts with the assessor, solicits attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. No known history of behavioral problems. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience.

My foster writes: Charli is a sweet girl who has quite an interest for exploration! You'll find her examining every inch of your home and following you around once she's comfortable with you. Charly was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her, and now this sweet girl is looking for a patient family to help her feel safe and loved. While new situations can be a little overwhelming for her, Charly has shown that she is capable of forming bonds and enjoys gentle, low-pressure interactions with people who give her the time she needs.

My Ideal Home
Charly would thrive in a calm home with someone who understands that confidence takes time. She will benefit from a predictable routine, slow introductions, and positive reinforcement training to help her feel more comfortable in new environments. Long walks, enrichment activities, and puzzle toys can help keep her mind busy and support her overall well-being.

Good with Other Pets?
Charly has shown interest in playing with other dogs while on walks and does not react negatively to dogs in her care center assessments. Slow, thoughtful introductions are recommended to help her feel comfortable with any future furry friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Charly's fearful nature and preference for approaching people on her own terms, she would do best in a home without children.

Things to Know
Charly is a sensitive girl who may need a little extra patience while adjusting to her new surroundings. Pre-Screener Form

Choco Bean was surrendered by his previous owner due to behavior concerns in the home. His previous family described him as a very affectionate and playful dog with them. He enjoys playing tug of war, his favorite treats are freeze-dried beef liver, and he has a very high energy level. Choco Bean is reported to guard food and toys and will hover and growl if approached while he is eating or playing. He is also noted to jump up persistently and pull hard on walks. He has also displayed leash-biting behaviors in the kennel when being removed, once out of the kennel, and when attempting to conduct a handling assessment. Chop was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him and is ready to find a fresh start with a family of his own. This handsome boy has a medium energy level and loves spending time with his people, whether it's heading out for a walk, playing with his favorite rope toys, or hopping in the car for an adventure. He's ready to chop his way right into your heart!

My Ideal Home
Chop would love an adopter who can provide daily walks, enrichment, and plenty of positive reinforcement. He enjoys staying active but also appreciates a predictable routine to help him feel confident. Puzzle toys, appropriate chew toys, and fun training sessions will keep both his mind and body happy.

Good with Other Pets?
Chop's previous family shared that he was friendly with unfamiliar dogs on leash, but he has shown that he can be uncomfortable around some dogs in the shelter environment. Slow introductions to dog friends are recommended, and dog parks are not the best fit for him. He also chased cats on walks with his previous owner, so a home without cats or small animals is recommended.

Good with Kids?
An adult only home is recommended for Chop. He can be sensitive about having his paws handled, especially during nail trims, and will do best with adopters who can respect his boundaries while helping him build positive associations through reward based training.

Things to Know
Chop is housetrained, enjoys car rides, and isn't picky when it comes to treats, making training extra rewarding. His previous family shared that he sometimes chewed on shoes, so providing plenty of appropriate chew toys and enrichment will help keep him on the right paw. He may need a little time to settle into new situations, but with patience and kindness, this sweet boy is sure to shine.

Chop is enrolled in our Shelter Scholar program and is blossoming with every training session. He is working on learning to relax on a mat, which is helping him find his calm and feel settled no matter the environment. With patience and positive reinforcement, Chop is developing the confidence and composure he needs to truly thrive. What my friends at ACC say about me:

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Clove!
Clove arrived to us as a stray with no ID. He's a sensitive, shy sweetheart who prefers to take his time connecting - he often approaches on his own terms and enjoys coming for pets when he feels ready. Clove is thoughtful and steady, and he's participating in our Shelter Scholars mat work program to help him decompress and build confidence in busy or new settings.

My Ideal Home
A calm, predictable adult-only home where a patient adopter can continue confidence-building work with slow, gentle handling. Clove does best with predictable routines, gentle enrichment, and gradual introductions to new people and situations. Training that focuses on cooperative care, impulse control, and loose-leash skills (and use of appropriate equipment like a front‑clip harness) will help him thrive.

Good with Kids?
No - Clove would do best in a home with only adults. He can be fearful and has nipped when frightened, so we recommend no children (under 13) while he continues to build confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
Unknown history with household pets. In shelter assessments he has ignored dogs in crates and remained calm during some introductions, though he can hold a tense frame during new encounters. Slow, controlled, supervised introductions are recommended and may help him feel comfortable around other dogs.

Leash Manners
Clove can be strong on leash and is known to mouth or leash-bite at times. He would benefit from loose-leash training, impulse-control exercises, and redirection with high-value treats or toys. Techniques like stop-and-go, direction changes, and a front‑clip harness will be useful while his handler builds engagement and focus.

Overall Health
Healthy overall; neutered and microchipped, and receiving routine veterinary care while in our care.

Behavior Determination
Experienced Adopters - Clove is sensitive and can show fearful or anxious reactions when stressed. He needs an adopter who understands fear-based behavior, can move slowly, avoid sudden approaches, and follow a behavior plan that includes desensitization, enrichment, and cooperative handling. This approach will help reduce anxiety and build his confidence over time.

Other Fun Facts
Clove is soft-bodied and affectionate once he trusts you - he often leans into gentle touch and takes treats nicely. He enjoys mat work to settle his body and mind, and he can be playful with toys (he sometimes grabs a toy and keeps it). Because he prefers to call the shots, many of his best moments come when you let him come to you for attention. His adoption fee has been reduced to help him find the home he deserves. A volunteer writes: It's not always easy to find someone who sees you, really sees you, especially in a life that moves fast, but Cole and Desire (220276) have found each other and, seeing them cuddled together in their cubby, we're so happy they have. Brought to us from homes with many other cats, meeting new people isn't always at the top of their to-do list. Companion would do best in an experienced adult-only home that can support him with structure and patience, especially around outdoor distractions. He'll thrive with calm leadership and predictable routines while he builds confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
Companion can become stiff, vocal, and tense when seeing other dogs on walks, so he will need slow, controlled introductions and careful management in shared spaces.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for young children due to on-leash reactivity and his need for a calm, structured environment.

Things to Know
Companion is a more reserved dog who prefers to take in his surroundings before engaging. He may appear aloof at first, often focusing on sniffing and observing rather than interacting. While he accepts handling and walks politely without pulling, he can become reactive when he sees other dogs and will need guidance and distance to feel comfortable. With time, patience, and consistent routines, he has the potential to become a steady, loyal companion.

Fun Fact

Cookie King was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him after first arriving at ACC as a stray. This sweet, treat-loving boy has quickly won over volunteers with his happy-go-lucky personality, wiggly greetings, and enthusiasm for making new friends. If you're looking for a dog who's always excited to spend time with you, Cookie King is ready to earn a permanent spot in your heart.

My Ideal Home
Cookie King would love an active home that can give him plenty of exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. He's an energetic boy who enjoys toys, treats, and staying busy, and he'll thrive with adopters who can help channel all of that excitement into fun adventures.

Good with Other Pets?
Cookie King gets very excited when he sees other dogs and can pull toward them to say hello. While shelter introductions have shown an enthusiastic greeting style, slow introductions to any resident dogs are recommended to help everyone feel comfortable.

Good with Kids?
ACC recommends a home with no children under 13 at this time.

Things to Know
Cookie King is a highly social dog who loves people and isn't shy about showing it. He can become easily excited and may jump around or get a little over aroused during play and handling, but he's eager to engage and enjoys toys, treats, and being part of the action. He's a wonderful candidate for continued reward-based training that helps him learn calm manners while keeping his fun-loving spirit intact.

What Volunteers Say
"What's a wonderful guy like this doing in a pop-up crate in the hallway when there is so much fun to be had in the world?" Volunteers describe Cookie King as an incredibly sweet dog who has everyone rooting for him. He's affectionately known as "treat obsessed," happily accepting just about any snack, and they'd love to see him put on a little healthy weight. One volunteer's wish is simple: come take him for a walk... and then keep walking all the way home.

Corazón was found tied to a light post and is now safe in our care, slowly learning that the world can feel a little softer and kinder. True to her name, she's a gentle "little heart" who is starting to show her sweet personality as she warms up to new people and surroundings.

My Ideal Home
Corazón would do best in a calm, patient home that allows her to adjust at her own pace. She benefits from gentle structure, predictable routines, and positive reinforcement as she builds confidence. A quieter environment will help her feel secure while she continues to come out of her shell.

Good with Other Pets?
Corazón has shown neutral, polite behavior around other dogs in care, though her full history is unknown. Slow, thoughtful introductions would be ideal if she were to live with another pet.

Good with Kids?
Due to her initial fearfulness and need for a slow, predictable environment, Corazón would do best in a home without very young children at this time.

Things to Know
Corazón is a soft, thoughtful girl who starts off a bit shy but becomes more comfortable with gentle encouragement. Once she trusts you, she allows handling, takes treats nicely, and shows calm, steady engagement. She will thrive with gradual desensitization to new environments and continued positive reinforcement training to build her confidence. With time, patience, and kindness, she has all the makings of a truly loving companion.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes: Corazón is exactly the kind of dog who quietly wins your heart. At first, she takes a moment to take in her surroundings, but once she feels safe, she gently comes forward for pets and leans into calm attention. She enjoys soft interaction, takes treats politely, and shows her sweet, sensitive side when given time to relax. Her name means "heart," and it fits her perfectly. She may not rush into love, but she gives it in the most sincere, meaningful way once she's ready.

Fun Fact
Corazón is proof that the quietest dogs often have the biggest hearts, they just need the right person to hear them. Crown would do best in an active home that can provide structure, consistency, and ongoing training. He will benefit from guidance around impulse control and calm greetings, along with regular outlets for his energy. An adopter who enjoys training and staying engaged with their dog will be a great fit.

Good with Other Pets?
Crown has shown no reactivity toward other dogs in care and may do well with compatible companions. As always, slow introductions and supervision are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Crown is recommended for a home without young children under 5 due to his tendency to jump up when excited.

Crown is strong on leash and will need continued training to build loose-leash walking skills. He can become excited and jump up for attention, but responds well to redirection and structure. With consistency, positive reinforcement, and enrichment, he has great potential to develop solid manners.

Brought to us from homes with many other cats, meeting new people isn't always at the top of their to-do list. They're a curious pair who would casually stroll toward me in the Free Roaming Room, choosing not to get particularly close, but, as we know, some cats don't always seek the company of people friends. They will allow some pets, but prefer to play, eat, and cuddle together. When Desire first came in, he would barely even touch the treats we offered in friendship. Staring at us in hopes it would help him to deduce our next move, he began to allow pets with the scratcher tool. Cole would sit with his paws out like a little frog, hopefully waiting for treats. Now they snuggle up together, confident in having done their part to make the Care Center a home as they wait for the next step of their journey to a forever home. Dexter was a bit shy when I first met him two days after his arrival at the care center. I could see, though that there was a lovely cat in him, just waiting to show for himself. I really like Dexter who might be less extroverted than Cairo but a cat with the promise to bring lots of love to his new family! Dexter is already neutered, seems reasonably healthy(he does have senior teeth, though) and his behavior evaluation is the witness of his initial weariness. Dexter's bag is ready.... What my friends at ACC say about me:

He was on top of the shelf, curious and interested in treats, and was easily coaxed down into the main kennel when offered more of them. He enjoyed all petting, leaning in gently for cheek rubs, and remained calm. He struggled when picked up, but he was reasonably tolerant of the experience and didn't escalate. After being set back down, he resumed his curious and sweet self.

Dexter interacts with the assessor, solicits & appreciates attention, is easy to handle and tolerates all petting. This cat is suitable for any level of adopter experience but should be counseled on his prior fearfulness..

I can go home today!

I have medical needs that staff will address with you when you meet me.

I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

Dipity is a male dog who was found alone in a park and brought to the shelter as a stray. He is still adjusting to new environments and benefits from time and space to feel comfortable. Once settled, he is able to move through his surroundings calmly with a steady, neutral presence.

Personality
Dipity is quiet and observant in new situations. He may not seek attention right away and can appear reserved when first approached. With gentle handling and patience, he is able to relax and tolerate interaction.

My Ideal Home
Dipity would do best in a calm, low-traffic home with a consistent routine. He will need patient adopters who can let him adjust at his own pace without pressure. A quiet environment will help him feel more secure over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Dipity's behavior around other dogs is still unclear. Slow, structured introductions and careful management would be needed in a home with other pets.

Good with Kids?
Dipity is recommended for a home without young children under 5 due to his fearful behavior. Older, respectful children may be considered after slow introductions.

Things to Know
Dipity walks well on leash and follows his handler with a calm, neutral body. He does best with slow introductions and a gentle, consistent approach. He benefits from patience as he continues to build confidence in new environments.

Fun Fact
Dipity is a quiet, thoughtful boy who takes his time to settle in, but shows a steady, calm presence once he feels comfortable.

He's the type of cat who may be too shy to ask for attention, but once it's offered, he's more than happy to soak it all up. Head scratches, chin rubs, full-body pets down his back-Eclipse isn't picky; if it's affection, it's all fair game for Eclipse once he's comfortable. He's also an absolute fiend for Churu and Temptations treats. Occasionally, he'll still pause mid-snack and look up at you with big cautious eyes as if to ask, "Is this okay?" For someone willing to give him a little patience and understanding, Eclipse is proof that some of the sweetest cats just need a little time to come out of the shadows.

Everyone nearby was laughing and smiling at her happiness. Afterward, we found a quiet patch of grass where she stretched out for the deepest nap, and it was so easy to picture her in a loving home, snoozing beside her person on a comfy couch. When she woke up, she lazily rested her chin in my hand. We finished the day with a pup cup, which she enjoyed with impressive enthusiasm. Years","type":"Dog","species":"Dog","link":"https://nycacc.app/browse/252921","gender":"Female","summaryHtml":"Meet Flo!
Flo came to the shelter after her owner lost housing and could no longer keep her. She was described as friendly and outgoing with people, but also as a sensitive girl who can become anxious and overwhelmed in new or busy environments. Once she feels comfortable, Flo is affectionate, social, and enjoys spending time with her people.

My Ideal Home
Flo is looking for a calm, predictable adult-only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She will do best with patient adopters who understand that confidence takes time and who are committed to using positive reinforcement and gentle guidance. A steady routine, quiet environment, and enrichment like sniffy walks and food puzzles will help her feel secure.

Good with Other Pets?
Flo enjoys familiar dog friends but can feel unsure and reactive around unfamiliar dogs. Because of this, she will need slow, careful introductions and is not a candidate for dog parks. With the right match and structure, she may do best as the only pet or with a very compatible, well-managed canine companion.

Good with Kids?
Flo would do best in an adult-only home while she builds confidence and continues working through her anxiety and handling sensitivities.

Things to Know
Flo is a thoughtful, sensitive dog who does best when the world feels predictable and calm. She may need time to warm up in new situations and can become overwhelmed by noise or fast movement. She has shown some anxiety and sensitivity around handling and change, but she also shows many positive qualities once she feels safe, including affection, engagement with her handler, and a willingness to connect. With patience, structure, and reward-based training, Flo has great potential to blossom into a steady and loving companion.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes: I'm taken by Flo the moment I meet her. She has the affect of a reserved wise elder, despite being only 3 years old, and everyone is friend. When she's not quietly snoozing, she's always happy to greet a visitor at her kennel, and on walks she's very engaged: checking in, making eye contact, sitting once she realizes a treat is coming her way, and calmly observing her environment. Her former guardian had wonderful things to say about her too, describing her as friendly and outgoing with people. Flo lived with another dog and is said to be playful around familiar dogs but nervous and reactive toward unfamiliar ones. Flo's story is a heartbreaking one. She arrived at the shelter when her person was fleeing a tumultuous situation and subsequently became homeless; the shelter did not allow pets. While they were hoping to reunite with Flo, ultimately they were unable to. She was clearly very loved by her former guardian, and we hope someone can honor their bond and provide her with the continued loving care she deserves. At the shelter, she's been social and affectionate with handlers. Her former guardian notes that she's scared of loud noises and fast-moving objects like skateboards, but she's shown a brave face in the shelter environment. Due to her anxiety and some handling sensitivities, she is recommended to an adult-only home. Flo is enrolled in our Shelter Scholar program and is making wonderful progress every single day. She is working on leave it, a skill that is helping her build focus and self-control in any situation. She is apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she appears wary of human contact. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

"Spirit cats" in a shelter context refer to cats who are very shy with people, preferring to live in a quiet environment and interacting with other cats rather than humans. They are often a good choice for patient, kind individuals who can create a safe and comfortable space for them to thrive. We cannot be certain whether or not Fork will warm up to socialization in shelter or in a home environment and clients should be counseled on the potential of Fork being a Spirit Cat.

A volunteer writes: Fork came to us from a home with many other cats, but without a lot of detailed information about who he is. She bravely sniffs but pulls back when we try too many pets and things. A volunteer writes: Goliath doesn't know what imposter syndrome is and he doesn't need to. This fellow searched far and wide for a family and while he didn't quite manage to find one on his own, he did find an approach that worked. It's called fake it 'til you make it and sitting on a porch corner walking himself into a Good Samaritan's house several times was just the thing he needed to do to convince them he belonged somewhere and with someone. Goliath is silly and sociable, greeting me from underneath his little blanket fort and then hopping on top of it to play. A friendly guy, he leaned into my hand as he made his laps around his condo. I'd love to learn more from Goliath and maybe even take a page from his book but what he really needs is to find you.

**Behavior Summary - Goliath** Goliath is a gentle, shy cat who has shown steady progress in building confidence during his time in the shelter. Initially very cautious and easily startled by unfamiliar sounds and activity, he often preferred to observe from a safe distance and would retreat when feeling uncertain. Despite his nervousness, Goliath consistently demonstrated curiosity about people and was willing to engage when approached calmly and respectfully. Over time, Goliath has become increasingly comfortable with human interaction. He now readily approaches to sniff offered hands, enjoys chin and cheek rubs, leans into petting, and has shown growing tolerance for handling. While he may still occasionally pull away when feeling unsure, he often re-engages once given a moment to process the interaction. His body language suggests that he wants social contact but benefits from being allowed to set the pace and choose when to participate. Goliath remains a somewhat sensitive cat who may need time to adjust to new environments and routines. He is likely to thrive in a calm home with patient adopters who can provide him with the space and reassurance needed to build trust. As his confidence grows, he has shown the potential to become a sweet and affectionate companion who enjoys gentle attention and close relationships with his people.

This animal has a little extra support from Bond Vet! Adopt this cutie and receive $1000 in your Bond Vet account to get their vet care started on the right foot.

Grizelda would thrive with an active family who enjoys including their dog in everyday adventures. Good with Kids?

Grizelda is described as social, affectionate, playful, and always ready for cuddles. She is housetrained, enjoys car rides, and is comfortable with bathing and brushing. Harlem was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him, and now this handsome, affectionate boy is ready to find his next forever family. He's a social, playful dog with a big heart, a love for belly rubs, and plenty of personality. Bonus points if you speak Spanish because Harlem knows tricks in both English and Spanish. Talk about a bilingual best friend!

My Ideal Home
Harlem is looking for an active home that can keep both his body and mind engaged. He enjoys walks, enrichment activities like food puzzles and long-lasting chews, and loves learning with positive reinforcement. After a day of adventures, he's just as happy to stretch out for belly rubs and relax with his favorite people.

Good with Other Pets?
Harlem should be the only pet in a home without cats or other small animals, as he has a history of chasing them on walks. Slow introductions to other dogs may be possible, but dog parks are not recommended.

Good with Kids?
Harlem would do best in a home without children under 13.

Things to Know
Harlem is an affectionate, intelligent dog who loves spending time with his people. He's crate trained, enjoys car rides, and already knows several cues, making him a wonderful companion for someone looking for a dog with a great foundation. He can become excited around high-value items, so continuing positive reinforcement training and providing appropriate enrichment will help him thrive. With his sweet nature and goofy charm, Harlem is ready to make himself right at home.

BoroughBuddy Notes
A BoroughBuddy writes: Harlem is a move-in ready dog! He is gentle and wonderful on a leash. We encountered many pigeons, squirrels, and kids and Harlem was unfazed. He is a very mellow dog. If you stand in one spot for more than a minute, he'll happily settle down by your feet. One of his cutest quirks is celebrating with joyful rolls on the ground whenever he's happy. Although he wasn't able to play with other dogs, he showed polite interest with an adorable play bow. He loves pets, snuggles, and taking his time to read and respond to all the neighborhood "pee-mails." Harlem is ready to be someone's loyal adventure buddy and couch companion all in one. Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! Hercules is a friendly and social dog who was abandoned by his previous owner and later surrendered to the shelter. He is a laid-back and affectionate dog once he feels comfortable but can be nervous in new situations. Hercules enjoys being around people and can be playful and wiggly when he bonds with someone.

My Ideal Home
Hercules would do best in an adult-only home with a calm, predictable environment. He needs a family that is patient and experienced with fearful or anxious dogs. He may display some nervousness or fear-based behaviors, so a home where he can adjust at his own pace will be ideal. His new family should be prepared to provide enrichment, structure, and positive reinforcement to help him manage his impulsivity and destructive tendencies.

Good with Kids?
No. Due to his fearfulness, especially around strangers, Hercules is better suited to a home without children under 13.

Good with Other Pets?
No. Hercules has not been tested with other animals but has shown fear-based behaviors (barking, growling, hiding) around cats. He would do best in a home with no cats or other pets.

Leash Manners
Hercules walks on a loose leash but can pull moderately. While he is generally easy to leash, he may be hesitant about collaring, and desensitization could help him feel more comfortable during walks.

Behavior Determination
Level 4. Hercules is recommended for an experienced adopter. His fearfulness and destructive behaviors, along with his poor impulse control, make him best suited for someone with experience working with anxious dogs. He will need a patient and dedicated adopter who can provide consistent training and care.

Other Fun Facts
Hercules is a sweet, affectionate dog who enjoys attention once he feels comfortable. He can be playful and social with those he bonds with, but he's also independent. He loves being near his humans, especially when treats are involved, and he seeks out attention on his own terms. Hercules is generally a calm dog but may need some extra time to adjust to his new home.

Jack is a handsome, affectionate pup looking for an experienced family who can help him continue building confidence and learning new skills. While Jack has had some big changes in his life recently, he has shown that he is a friendly guy who enjoys spending time with people and exploring the world around him. With patience, structure, and positive reinforcement, Jack is ready to find a home where he can thrive.

My Ideal Home
Jack would do best with an experienced adopter who understands canine body language and is committed to helping him practice calm behaviors. He is an active dog who will benefit from daily exercise, enrichment, and reward-based training. A predictable routine and patient approach will help Jack feel comfortable and set him up for success.

Good with Other Pets?
Jack has shown some interest in other dogs and has had positive moments meeting canine friends. However, he can become tense and fixate on dogs while on leash, so continued training and slow introductions will help him have successful interactions. A front-clip harness and positive reinforcement training can help him focus on his person during walks.

Good with Kids?
Due to Jack's tendency to become over-aroused and mouthy during exciting situations, an adult-only home is recommended. He would do best with someone who can recognize his communication signals and help him stay calm before he becomes overwhelmed.

Things to Know
Jack is a sweet dog who enjoys affection, but he prefers interactions on his own terms and appreciates slow introductions. His previous family reported that he can become overexcited and mouthy, especially during high-stress situations like grooming, so he will need continued work on impulse control and calm handling. Jack has shown that he can be a wonderful companion, and a patient adopter willing to help him succeed will have a loyal friend by their side.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes: Jack is perfect as far as we're concerned! He's gorgeous, kind, and friendly to everyone he meets. During outings, Jack has shown his gentle nature, calmly handling distractions and enjoying time with his people. He walks nicely on leash, appears housetrained, and is even a champion cuddler who loves sharing a bench with his favorite humans. Jack has so much love to give and is hoping someone will give him the chance to show them just how special he is. My#BoroughBreak Buddy writes: Jack was a good boy . He's big but well behaved .
