Jimmy was found wandering alone on the street and brought to a local precinct, where he was described as friendly during intake. This handsome boy has been social and people-oriented in care, and he's now looking for a home that can help him channel his enthusiasm into all the right outlets (especially if cheese is involved).

My Ideal Home
Jimmy would do well with an adopter who enjoys an active, playful dog and is ready to continue his training in a fun, positive way. He can get excited quickly and may grab or mouth the leash when amped up, so a home that can provide structure, enrichment, and reward-based training will help him shine. He'll thrive with consistency, clear boundaries, and plenty of engaging activities to keep his mind busy.

Good with Other Pets?
Jimmy has shown polite, neutral interest in another dog at the care center during a supervised introduction. His overall history with other animals is unknown, so slow, thoughtful introductions would be important if living with another pet.

Good with Kids?
Due to some observed guarding behavior around valued items and his tendency to get excited quickly, Jimmy is recommended for a home without children under 13 at this time.

Things to Know
Jimmy is a bright, affectionate boy who loves engagement with his people and especially enjoys toys, play, and tasty rewards (cheese might be his love language). He'll do best with calm guidance and positive reinforcement training. He has shown potential for guarding high-value items, so ongoing trade-up games and teaching cues like "drop it" will help set him up for success. With structure and patience, Jimmy has a great foundation to become a fun and loyal companion.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes: Jimmy is a classically handsome boy with a classic name. He waits patiently in his kennel and greets me with a soft, sweet expression that makes it easy to like him right away. Once outside, he lights up during play, especially with a favorite octopus toy he happily brings back over and over, dropping it into my lap to start the game again. He's social and people oriented, and during his time in care he's shown how much he enjoys interaction and enrichment. He also has a very relatable quirk: a strong appreciation for cheese, which may or may not have made a surprise appearance during his assessment. Jimmy is a fun, engaging dog who will shine in a home that can match his energy and continue helping him build good manners through positive reinforcement.

In just a short time frame with his foster, he opens up more and more each day. This Halloween cat, with his black coat and yellow eyes, is definitely a night owl. You can hear him playing with multiple toys, running around, munching on food, and climbing all over. He's very hesitant around new people, and takes his time warming up, but who doesn't? Jordan came to ACC from a home with more than 40 cats after his owner became ill. With so many animals and so little individual interaction, he didn't have many opportunities to build confidence around people. Here at the shelter, Jordan is a very shy, quiet boy who prefers to stay tucked into his cubby. He tolerates gentle petting and is beginning to relax during calm interactions, sometimes closing his eyes softly as he adjusts to attention.

My Ideal Home
Jordan will thrive in a calm, patient home with adults who understand shy or under-socialized cats. He needs a quiet environment, predictable routines, and a safe space to retreat to while he slowly acclimates. Treats, soft voices, and low-pressure interactions will help him build trust over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Likely yes. Jordan previously lived with many cats and may benefit from a calm, well-socialized resident cat who can model positive interactions with people. Slow introductions are important so he doesn't feel pressured.

Other Fun Facts
Jordan is a thoughtful little observer who watches quietly from his safe spot. As he warms up, he leans gently into cheek rubs and shows moments of comfort that hint at the companionship he could offer once he feels safe. For adopters who enjoy helping a shy cat blossom, Jordan is a rewarding, heartfelt project and a sweet soul waiting for his first true home.

Jujubee was found near a school and is a young, social, and enthusiastic girl who is always ready to engage with her people. She has a bright, friendly personality and loves staying close to her handler, showing lots of interest in attention and interaction.

My Ideal Home
Jujubee would do best in an active home that can provide daily physical exercise, mental stimulation, and structure. She will thrive with enrichment like food puzzles, long-lasting chews, and interactive games to help channel her energy in positive ways.

Good with Other Pets?
Jujubee has been observed to ignore other dogs on walks and showed a soft, polite greeting during a controlled introduction. Slow, supervised introductions are always recommended for any resident pets.

Good with Kids?
Due to her high energy and jumpy, enthusiastic greetings, ACC recommends a home without very young children (under 5). Older children who are comfortable around active dogs may be a good fit after meeting her.

Things to Know
Jujubee is highly social and affectionate, often seeking out her handlers for attention and physical closeness. She can be very enthusiastic, including jumping up and rolling over during interactions, so she will benefit from consistent, reward-based training to build manners and impulse control. She enjoys engaging play, follows her handler readily, and responds well to positive interaction. With structure, enrichment, and continued guidance, she has all the makings of a fun and loving companion.

Fun Fact
Jujubee doesn't just like attention, she actively seeks it out, making her a cheerful, people-loving pup who's always ready to be part of the action. Kali is an owner surrender who is now looking for a fresh start and a home where she can settle in and feel secure. She has a calm, easy presence and does best when life feels predictable and kind of low-key, which helps her confidence really shine through.

Personality
Kali is a steady, people-oriented girl who likes being part of whatever her humans are doing. She's not pushy for attention, but she enjoys staying close, checking in, and quietly taking in her surroundings. Her foster describes her as an easy dog in the home who settles well once she understands the routine and enjoys just being included in daily life.

She responds really well to calm energy and kind handling. Nothing overly complicated, just a consistent, relaxed environment where she knows what to expect.

Out and About
Kali is a super nice leash walker with no pulling and no reactivity toward people. She moves along at an easy pace and stays soft even when passing other dogs, often with a loose body and a friendly, wagging tail. Walks with her feel pretty straightforward and relaxed, like she's just happy to be out and about with you.

Social Behavior
Kali is moderately social when meeting new people and will usually approach when called. She tends to stay nearby and then drift around the room a bit before coming back to check in. She's comfortable with gentle handling and does best when interactions stay calm and unforced.

At the shelter she greeted another dog with a loose, wiggly body, then casually disengaged and went back to focusing on her handler, showing a nice ability to take things in stride.

Home Life
Kali would do really well in a home that has a steady routine and a calm vibe. Her foster describes her as an easy companion who enjoys being part of everyday life without needing constant stimulation. She's happiest when things feel balanced and predictable and she can just hang out with her people.

Things to Know
Kali is comfortable with normal handling and day to day environments, and she does best when people are gentle and not overly intense with her. She's the kind of dog who settles in nicely once she understands the rhythm of a home.

Fun Fact
Kali is a quiet "stick by your side" kind of dog. She doesn't ask for much, she just likes being near her people, keeping things calm, and being part of the moment. 🐾

Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Keto!
He can be shy at first and appreciates slow, calm introductions to new people and places. Keto enjoys attention on his own terms - he seeks contact when he's comfortable, leans into people he trusts, and shows a soft, neutral wag when relaxed. Because he can be wary, moving at his pace and using treats and praise to build trust will help him settle in.

My Ideal Home
A calm, patient home where introductions to people and new routines are done slowly and respectfully. Keto would benefit from a family or adopter who understands canine body language and can give him predictable structure, consistent positive reinforcement, and daily mental and physical enrichment (long-lasting chews, food puzzles, games, and regular walks). A quieter household or one with older, respectful children will help him thrive.

Good with Kids?
No (not with very young children). Keto would do best without very young children under 5 due to his fearful/defensive tendencies. He may be open to meeting older children once he's had calm, supervised introductions.

Good with Other Pets?
Keto has greeted other dogs with some tension and vocalizing at the gate, so dog introductions should be slow and supervised. He's not strongly reactive on leash during assessments but would benefit from careful, controlled meet-and-greets. No reliable information about cats - assume unknown and introduce cautiously if considered.

Leash Manners
Keto shows mild pulling at times but follows a handler readily and responds well to movement and guidance. He can be distracted when loose in a new space, so short, positive training sessions on the leash and reward-based walks will help his confidence and focus.

Behavior Determination
Level 2 / Experienced or Patient Adopters - Keto has shown fearful or defensive behavior in some situations (barking/growling when first approached by officers). He needs adopters who will move slowly, use positive association techniques, and allow him to initiate interactions when he feels safe. No young children recommended.

Other Fun Facts
Keto loves to sniff and explore, follows his handler on short jogs, and will often lean in for contact once he trusts you. He responds well to calm encouragement and treats, and with a little patience he shows a sweet, affectionate side. Kingsley is a handsome senior gentleman who's looking for a calm, understanding home to spend his golden years in. His previous owner described him as anxious when left alone, but also noted that he's easygoing with everyday handling and unbothered by things like being woken up, touched on his paws, or having his collar handled. At the shelter, Kingsley has been more reserved, preferring to sniff around quietly and politely approach for treats.

My Ideal Home
Kingsley would do best in a patient, lower-key home where he can settle in at his own pace and enjoy a predictable routine. He's looking for adopters who understand that sometimes the sweetest companions are the quiet ones.

Good with Other Pets?
Kingsley has shown neutral behavior around other dogs at the shelter, though his previous owner noted that he may guard food or treats around other dogs. Careful management around high value items and slow introductions are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to Kingsley's reported resource guarding, ACC recommends a home with older, respectful children who can follow his boundaries or an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Kingsley is a more independent guy who enjoys exploring at his own pace and is especially motivated by treats. He can become uncomfortable with prolonged handling and may show subtle signs like lip licking or tensing when unsure, so he'll do best with people who respect his space and communication. Kingsley may also experience some anxiety when left alone and would benefit from patience, enrichment, and a calm environment as he adjusts to home life again.

A volunteer writes: When I look at Kingsley's frost-kissed muzzle, I see a testament to the 9 years he spent loving and being loved, until housing insecurity made him lose everything he knew. Kobe is a social and affectionate dog who was surrendered when his owners could no longer care for him due to housing insecurity. He loves being near people and enjoys simple pleasures like car rides, water, and chew time with his favorite toys and bones.

My Ideal Home
Kobe would do best in a calm, structured adult-only home where he can feel secure and understood. He is house trained, enjoys a routine of daily walks, and already knows cues like his name and "stay." He will thrive with patient, force free training that helps him build confidence and reinforce calm behaviors.

Good with Other Pets?
He is recommended as a single pet home and should not visit dog parks. He will do best as the only animal in the home.

Good with Kids?
Due to fear responses and sensitivities observed in care, Kobe is recommended for an adult-only home at this time.

Things to Know
Kobe is a medium energy dog who enjoys walks and engagement with his people, but he can become fearful in unfamiliar or stressful situations. He may pull on leash and can react to other dogs, so he will need supportive equipment like a front clip harness and ongoing positive reinforcement training. He also shows strong interest in toys and can become protective of them, so trade up games and teaching a "drop" cue will be important. Kobe is sensitive to handling at times, especially around restraint or touch of his paws and collar, so a slow, choice based approach will help him feel safe. With structure, patience, and consistency, Kobe has a lot of potential to be a loving and loyal companion.

Fun Fact
Kobe's favorite thing in the world might be a good chew toy followed closely by a car ride adventure with his favorite person. Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! My foster writes: Ladybug? More like Cuddle-bug! Meet Ladybug, a really special girl with an endless amount of love to give. Once you start petting her and she looks up at you with her beautiful brown eyes, and starts purring as she melts into your arms, you'll never want to stop! She might be a little hesitant at first, but with just a little love and reassurance, Ladybug blossoms into the sweetest, cuddliest, adorably playful dog. Most of time, Ladybug is a sleepy, docile couch potato, and is impressively gentle taking treats, pawing, and giving affection, but she also has a fun, silly, energetic streak! Don't be surprised to catch her zooming around the room to celebrate a particularly good cuddle session or meal, or to initiate play mid-day! And if you're looking for a new running partner, don't count Ladybug out! She is quite the athlete and will also be an excellent exercise companion. She's still working on getting all of the basic commands down, but she is responsive and highly engaged during training sessions. While we don't know too much about Ladybug's past, her almost magnetic pull to the couch (no invite needed!) and stellar potty training suggest that she may have once had a home. My other foster writes: Ladybug is a brindle queen waiting for her forever home! She is beaming with love, and is as energy fueled as she is a master in cuddling (naps with her are sure to improve your life). Ladybug will do best in a consistently social environment without prolonged alone time. cannot be left alone for long periods of time due to her anxiety. Ladybug needs a patient owner who can continue to work through her anxieties, helping build her confidence and trust around strangers. My Borough Breaker writes: When I brought Ladybug home for a short foster stint, she literally started jumping for joy! Ladybug was found roaming the streets alone and is still learning that the world can be a safe place. She does best with people who let her come forward at her own pace.

Personality
Ladybug is cautious at first and can feel overwhelmed in new situations. She may prefer to observe from a distance before engaging, but she is gentle and non-reactive, and she benefits from calm, steady companionship. Once she feels secure, her softer personality starts to come through.

My Ideal Home
Ladybug would thrive in a quiet, low-traffic home with patient adopters who understand the value of letting her set the pace. She will do best with a calm routine and gentle encouragement rather than pressure. A peaceful environment will help her confidence grow over time.

Good with Other Pets?
Ladybug has not been comfortable passing other dogs closely and may feel overwhelmed in busy or high-energy interactions. With slow, thoughtful introductions and proper management, she may be able to adjust, but she will need space and patience while she builds confidence.

Good with Kids?
Ladybug would do best in a home without young children under 5. She is sensitive to her environment and will thrive best in a calm, predictable household.

Things to Know
Ladybug walks nicely on leash without pulling but is still building confidence outside the shelter. She benefits from slow introductions, consistency, and a gentle approach that allows her to explore the world at her own pace. Small moments of trust go a long way with her.

Fun Fact
Ladybug may be a little shy at first, but once she starts to feel safe, she really starts to "bug" for attention in the sweetest way. With time, she's the kind of lucky charm who quietly lands in your heart. 🐞

Lenny is a 5-year-old girl who was found running loose on the street and is now at ACC looking for a calm, patient home where she can finally feel safe and settle in. She can be shy in new situations, but once she relaxes, her gentle, affectionate personality starts to come through.

Personality
Lenny is a sensitive, quiet girl who takes her time getting comfortable with new people and places. At first she may seem unsure, but with patience she begins to settle, seek reassurance, and lean into gentle contact. Once she trusts you, she enjoys affection and often shows her softer side by resting her head on people for comfort.

Out and About
Lenny walks with a loose leash and a steady pace. She does not react to people or other dogs she passes and generally follows her handler calmly. She benefits from predictable routines and gentle guidance, especially in busier environments where she may initially feel overwhelmed.

Social Behavior
In new environments, Lenny may be hesitant at first, but she softens with time and reassurance. She allows petting once comfortable and often responds to calm interaction by settling into a seated position and leaning into touch. Her comfort grows best when she is given space to approach things at her own pace.

Home Life
Lenny will do best in an adult only, single pet home that can offer patience, consistency, and a calm environment. Slow introductions to new people and places will help her continue building confidence. She has strong potential to become a loyal, steady companion once she feels secure.

Things to Know
Lenny has medical needs that staff will discuss with adopters. She thrives with gentle, force-free handling and will do best in a home that understands shy dogs and allows her to progress at her own pace.

Fun Fact
Lenny may be reserved at first, but once she feels safe, she becomes a quiet, comforting companion who just wants to stay close and lean in for affection. 🐾

A volunteer writes: Twins Leo and Lex, two handsome Gingers were brought to us as their family moved to a place not allowing pets. A little bit more time seems to be needed to get Lex out of his shell. May be it could be with you? I bet his brother Leo would love to be adopted with him.....

Found as a stray and brought to the 90th Precinct before coming to ACC, this affectionate city walker is ready to trade kennel noise for cozy naps and neighborhood strolls. Volunteers rave about her sweet manners and cuddle game on BoroughBreaks. My Ideal Home An experienced, adult-only home that offers calm structure, patience, and a thoughtful decompression plan. Routine sniffy walks, enrichment (food puzzles, long-lasting chews), and reward-based training will help her shine. A front-clip harness and clear, consistent cues set her up for success. Good with Kids? Recommended adult-only (no children under 13) based on shelter observations and behavior team guidance. Good with Other Pets? Best as the only dog for now. In the busy kennel room she can be reactive (barking/lunging), but outdoors-with space and support-she often passes dogs without fuss. No dog parks. If you have a resident dog, plan slow, structured introductions with professional guidance. Potatoes needs a home without cats or small animals. Leash Manners Often a loose, thoughtful walker who checks in with her handler. If excited, she may briefly grab the leash; this has been easy to redirect with treats or a squeaker. She's tolerant of gentle petting during walk breaks and navigates sidewalks well when supported. Overall Health Spayed. Vet team notes dental tartar; regular dental care, balanced diet, and everyday exercise will help her feel her best. Previously had a shelter cough that resolved. (Your vet can personalize her wellness plan once home.) Behavior Determination & Other ACC Behavior Level: 3 Recommendations: Adult-only; no dog parks; front-clip harness; reward-based training to build focus around other dogs. In kennel/play-yard settings she may react toward neighboring dogs; on the street, distance and support help her stay composed. Fun Facts Her BoroughBreak buddies called her "an absolute angel" with "paw-tastic manners." Car-ride comfy, picnic-ready, generous with kisses, and a champion at settling after a good walk. Ready to meet Load O' Potatoes? If you love training, structure, and cuddly couch time-and you're ready to be her safe landing-Lo's your girl. My #BoroughBreak Buddy Writes: Lo was an absolute angel and pawtastic! She was very well-behaved and had great manners. She is very sweet and gave loads of kisses! She was never hesitant and was always ready for the next adventure! A Volunteer Wrote: I first met her flat on her back. She had thrown herself down, in a fit of pleasure, on the sidewalk, and was scratching her back on the cement and wriggling around and wagging her tail, while her borough break buddy looked equally delighted. "She's just the best!" she reported in on her morning with our girl. She's endlessly affectionate, has fantastic manners, and is adored by all of us because she's been here long enough for us all to fall in love. Lucy came to us after living her life as a beloved indoor companion and is now looking for a quiet home where she can settle in and be cherished once again. She may be a little shy at first, but beneath her timid exterior is an affectionate lap cat who enjoys gentle attention and forms close bonds with the people she trusts. With a little patience, Lucy's sweet and loving personality is sure to shine.

My Ideal Home
Lucy would thrive in a calm, low-traffic home with adopters who understand that she may need a little time to adjust. She enjoys cozy places to relax, gentle play sessions, and spending time with her favorite people. A family willing to let her settle in at her own pace will be rewarded with a loyal and affectionate companion.

Good with Kids?
Lucy has no history of living with children. Because she can be timid in new situations, a home with older, respectful children or adults is recommended.

Good with Other Pets?
Lucy has no known experience living with cats or dogs. If introduced to other pets, slow and gradual introductions would be recommended.

Overall Health
Lucy has moderate to severe dental disease, is FIV positive, has a heart murmur with no current clinical disease, and is suspected to have a chronic geriatric condition. She is also overweight. Our staff can discuss what this means for her future care.

Behavior Determination
Level 2 - Lucy is a gentle, affectionate cat who has shown signs of stress in the shelter environment but continues to welcome gentle petting and attention. She will do best with adopters who can give her time to adjust and understand that fearful behavior in the shelter does not reflect the loving companion she has been in a home.

Other Fun Facts
Lucy is a true cuddle bug! She loves being brushed, enjoys being picked up and held, happily accepts belly rubs, and has been described as a quiet lap cat who enjoys hide-and-seek, stuffed toys, window watching, and even baths. Her previous family's favorite things about her were just how sweet, loving, and cuddly she is. Lulu was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her, and she is now hoping for a fresh start with someone who understands her big personality, big feelings, and big heart. She's social, playful, and full of energy, with a clear love for people and engagement.

My Ideal Home
Lulu would do best with a patient, experienced adopter who can help her work through anxiety, build confidence, and provide structure. She benefits from a calm, predictable environment, consistent routines, and reward-based training. Enrichment like sniffy walks, chew toys, and mental games will help her channel her energy in positive ways.

Good with Other Pets?
Lulu has shown mixed signals around other dogs, including both interest and uncertainty. Because of this, slow and careful introductions are recommended, and she may do best as the only pet or with structured introductions to compatible dogs. She is not recommended for dog parks.

Good with Kids?
Due to her anxiety, mouthiness, and occasional conflict around handling, Lulu would do best in a home without young children.

Things to Know
Lulu is an active, affectionate girl who can be both enthusiastic and sensitive. She may become anxious or vocal in new situations and benefits from slow introductions and positive reinforcement. She has some house soiling and leash challenges that will improve with consistency and routine. She loves car rides, toys, water play, and spending time with people she trusts. With patience, Lulu's loving and playful personality really shines through.

Volunteer Notes
A volunteer writes: Lulu is a girl that quickly steals my heart. We met her about a month or so ago for the first time. She had been high energy and a little unsure of her surroundings. Since then, she had been adopted and returned, went to adoption events, and became a volunteer favorite. In the yard, Lulu easily leans into pets, even getting a bit of belly rubs in! Lulu came to us for the first time last year when her owner was arrested. She was quickly reclaimed by her family. This year, when her family was moving out of state, Lulu was surrendered with the hopes of finding a new family for her. Lulu has been stressed at the shelter, as many dogs are. She is high energy, but seeks comfort in people. She can be conflicted with getting pet - she leans in but sometimes jumps away. Lulu does not like going back into her kennel, and often lays down when approaching her room. Our volunteers have accompanied her to events, and they said Lulu was "beyond perfect." Lulu was adopted, but returned when her adopter was uncomfortable with Lulu's mouthy behavior. Lulu is described as social, active, and playful. She loves car rides, braided toys, and cuddling. She had been crate trained for up to 5 hours, loves water and bath times, and had been playful with familiar and unfamiliar dogs. Madame Jenny, also known as MJ, is a long stay pup with a reduced adoption fee and a whole lot of love to give. She has been in foster care for a few years now, and during that time her foster has watched her grow into a confident, social, and deeply affectionate senior dog who is truly ready for her forever home.

Personality
MJ is playful, smart, and full of charm. She enjoys engaging with people and has a joyful, affectionate nature that makes her very easy to fall in love with. She can be a little cautious with new people at first, but it does not take her long to warm up and show her loving side. Once she feels safe, she is social, engaging, and very people oriented.

Home Life
MJ is an active senior who still enjoys play and daily walks. She loves games like tug of war and enjoys going out for walks where she can trot happily alongside her person. She is also very affectionate and enjoys quiet time close to her people.

She is intelligent and enjoys learning, especially when training is paired with patience and positive reinforcement. She continues to benefit from structure and consistency in her routine.

Social Behavior
According to her foster, MJ can do well with other dogs and even cats when introduced slowly and at her own pace.

She may be a bit reserved when meeting strangers, but she warms up and becomes affectionate once she feels safe. She enjoys connection with people and thrives in environments where she feels secure and understood.

My Ideal Home
MJ will do best in an adult home where she can be the center of attention and enjoy a calm, stable environment. She would thrive with someone who appreciates a loving companion who enjoys both playtime and quiet bonding moments.

She needs continued guidance around resource guarding, as she does not always like to share food, toys, or bedding. A patient, experienced adopter who can provide structure and positive reinforcement will help her continue to succeed.

Fun Fact
MJ's foster says one of her most special traits is her intuition. She always seems to know when her person needs comfort, whether they are feeling down or just in need of a little extra affection. She is the kind of dog who naturally shows up at exactly the right moment, offering love, presence, and a calming energy that makes her truly unforgettable.

What my friends at ACC say about me:

I am a shy, older gentleman, looking for the perfect forever home!

I am a cat that is in need of a lap! I can't wait to be your new lap cat.

I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!

I have been known to shower my favorite people in love!

I am finding the shelter a little overwhelming, but when it's just you and me and some peace and quiet you'll see what a love bug I am.

I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

A volunteer writes: With a hopeful kitty smile, Mandarin made his way over to the front where he nuzzled the door and lowered his head to sweetly headbutt my hand. Meet Marble Swirl!
Marble Swirl is a handsome brindle boy with an even more beautiful personality. Found tied up in a stairwell, he hasn't let his past dim his bright spirit. From the moment he arrived at ACC, Marble Swirl has been friendly, affectionate, and eager to make new friends. He loves being with people and is always ready to greet you with a loose, wiggly body and a happy smile.

My Ideal Home
Marble Swirl would love a home where he can be part of the family and enjoy plenty of quality time with his people. Whether it's neighborhood walks, learning new tricks, or relaxing together after a fun day, he's happiest when he's included. He's an active but easygoing companion who will thrive with regular exercise, positive reinforcement training, and lots of affection.

Personality
Marble Swirl is the definition of a people dog. He is highly social, seeks out affection, and loves interacting with his handlers. During walks he stays close, walks nicely on leash, and happily checks in with his person. He's food-motivated, eager to learn, and has already shown he enjoys practicing cues like "touch." His enthusiasm sometimes leads to a few happy jumps for attention, but it's all part of his charming, affectionate nature.

Behavior Assessment
Marble Swirl has earned a Behavior Assessment Level 2. He is friendly, social, and enjoys meeting new people, but can become a little overexcited and may jump up when greeting handlers. Positive reinforcement training and reinforcing calm behaviors like "sit" will help him continue polishing his manners. Because of his enthusiasm, ACC recommends a home without very young children. He has also participated in dog introductions at the shelter, and adopters should plan slow, thoughtful introductions to any resident dogs.

Overall Health
Marble Swirl is neutered, microchipped, vaccinated, and ready for his new family. He was recently treated for a mild upper respiratory infection (doggy cold) and is recovering well. He also has mild dental tartar, but otherwise appears to be in good health.

Why You'll Love Him
Marble Swirl has all the makings of a wonderful companion-kind, affectionate, playful, and eager to connect with people. He's the type of dog who will happily walk by your side, lean in for pets, and remind you every day just how rewarding it is to open your heart to a shelter dog. Marbles was found tied up outside a building and is now looking for a calm, patient home where he can truly settle and feel safe.

My Ideal Home
We call him our "Velcro-dog" because once he has claimed you as his pack, he won't leave your side. Marbles would do well in a calm predictable adult-only home. He needs a patient adopter who will take the time to teach him how to be the best dog ever. Marbles is smart and highly motivated to please you. He just needs consistent positive reinforcement (and lots of exercise) to learn how to be your best buddy.

Good with Other Pets?
When on a leash, Marbles has shown neutral, polite behavior towards other dogs. If introducing him to other dogs in a household, it's highly recommended that you make a slow, thoughtful introduction over an extended period of time. He hasn't been around other pets and can be territorial.

Good with Kids?
He still has toddler tendencies and is a very physical dog. When he loves you, he loves you with his entire 50-pound body! He doesn't know his own strength, so we wouldn't recommend a household with children under 12 or anyone who can be knocked over easily.

Things to Know
Marbles is a tender-hearted boy who can feel overwhelmed in busy or high-stimulation environments, so he does best with calm handling and plenty of space to decompress. Once he feels safe, he enjoys gentle attention and will quietly seek out connection in his own way. He's still learning that the world isn't something to be worried about, and he benefits from slow, reassuring guidance.

Fun Fact
Once Marbles trusts you, he really starts to roll with affection and shows the sweetest little moments of leaning in like he's decided you're his safe place.

Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! Marcus arrived to Manhattan Animal Care Center as a stray with ID. His history is a mystery, but staff describe him as affectionate on his own terms - he loves attention but prefers slow introductions and gentle handling. Marcus can be sensitive around his head and neck, so he does best when people respect his boundaries and move at a calm, predictable pace.

My Ideal Home
A patient, calm home where his people understand canine body language and are willing to use force-free handling and positive reinforcement. Marcus will thrive with consistent daily mental and physical activity (walks, food puzzles, chew toys) and slow, low-pressure introductions to new people and places. A household without very young children is recommended; he may do well with older kids after proper meet-and-greets. Experience with dogs that are handling-sensitive is a plus.

Good with Kids?
Not recommended for very young children. Because Marcus can be sensitive to handling around his head and neck, a home without toddlers is best. He could be open to older children once he's had calm, supervised introductions.

Good with Other Pets?
Positive with other dogs in observed meetings - he greeted another dog with a soft body and wagging tail and even rested his head on the other dog's neck. Cat compatibility is unknown and would need careful, supervised introductions.

Leash Manners
Marcus follows his handler readily but can show moderate pulling. He responds well to guided walks and will benefit from continued loose-leash work and consistent, positive training to reinforce good walking manners.

Behavior Determination
Level 2 - Suitable for adopters who are comfortable with a dog that is handling-sensitive and who will commit to patient, force-free training and careful introductions. Not recommended for homes with very young children.

Other Fun Facts
Marcus is a big softie who leans into people and seeks contact on his terms. He becomes receptive to treats during handling, enjoys sniffing out toys, and can be vocal when someone knocks before happily greeting them with a wagging tail. He's affectionate, enjoys one-on-one attention, and shows friendly, social behavior with other dogs.

What my friends at ACC say about me:

Marley is an adult cat that may not have had many interactions with humans from an early age. She is apprehensive of people and while showing no aggressive behaviors, she appreciates some attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. Please be mindful that older cats will require more time and skill in order for them to be comfortable around people, we recommend offering high value treats and food to help build a positive association to humans. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

I have lived with cats in my previous home.

I am looking for a home with a patient person.

I can be slow to adjust to new environments. I prefer to take things at my own pace.

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

I'm sensitive and shy. I'll need extra help from you.

I came in with multiple cats and am currently housed with my sibling, Alex 226461 who I am bonded with! (as seen in photo)

A volunteer writes: Visiting with Alex (226461) and Marley makes me feel like I've walked into a play. Except both of these adorable cats seem to patiently and adorably look to us for their entertainment. With one paw delicately perched on the ledge of his bed, Alex waited for me to introduce myself before presenting his neck for some scritches. Marley, meanwhile, prefers her perch to being downstairs when there are guests but she really, really loves pets. The circumstances need to be just right (i.e., calm and quiet) and when they are, she very sweetly leans in. My Ideal Home
Marley would do best with an adopter who enjoys an active routine and is excited to help him build some basic manners. A calm, structured environment will support his continued progress as he gains confidence and strength.

Good with Other Pets?
Marley has limited history with other animals. In the shelter, he has shown difficulty during close dog greetings and may react strongly at first. He may do best as the only dog, or with slow, carefully managed introductions guided by an experienced adopter or trainer.

Leash Manners

Maxwell is on the at-risk list due to behavior concerns. In the prior home, Maxwell was reported to have bitten two people. In both incidents, he bit and immediately released after being approached and touched while asleep. Previous owner noted Maxwell is attentive, empathetic, and playful. Maxwell in the care center has been social and playful with staff. Medically, Maxwell is noted to be overweight and has recently recovered from CIRDC. Maxwell was surrendered by his previous owner due to them not being able to care for him any longer. His previous owner described him as a social, affectionate, active, playful, vocal, clingy dog. He would spend most of his time where people are, has been to the groomer, loves bath time/water, playing with balls, sitting in chairs, and loves boiled chicken. In his previous home, he would go on two 40-minute walks a day and had access to a patio. He is not crate trained. He sometimes enjoys car rides, and sometimes is very anxious in cars. Maxwell is noted to have a bite history. He escalated to biting his owner when they attempted to kiss him while he was asleep, and a neighbor who attempted to pet him while he was asleep. During his stay in care, Maxwell has been easy to remove from his crate and take on walks. He did show potential resource guarding of the toy during his handling assessment. Due to all noted concerns displayed in a home environment and in care, we recommend for Maxwell be placed with a New Hope placement partner who can provide an experienced adult-only foster home and provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home. He loves bathtime (we love a water dog) and going on long walks, plus he knows a handful of commands, including "sit," "stay," "paws," and "ball." He even knows to wait to have his paws cleaned after walks! He is said to be tolerant, friendly, outgoing, and playful around both familiar and unfamiliar dogs. At the shelter, Maxwell has been friendly and social with staff, and though you can usually find him sitting calmly in his crate, he gets excited for walks. On my first walk with him, a passerby commented on how cute he was, and I wasn't surprised. My foster writes: Meowy Dearest is a shy but curious sweetheart who loves enrichment toys and relaxing on her cat tree. She takes her time warming up, but once she does, she'll quietly hang out nearby and make herself right at home. This cute little void needs someone who's patient, but the bond is worth the wait. This petite little kitty has a quiet charm that wins hearts quickly. Meowy Dearest is naturally curious and observant-she likes to take in her surroundings carefully before deciding the best place to explore next. Once she feels comfortable, her playful side comes out and she'll happily chase toys, investigate every corner, and show off her gentle kitten energy. Though she can be a little cautious in new situations and with new people, she's incredibly sweet and affectionate once she settles in. She loves calm company and approaches once she feels secure. Her gentle personality makes her a peaceful companion. Meowy Dearest is quite confident with other cats and enjoys feline friends, making her a wonderful addition to a multi-cat household. 💛 Meet Meowy Dearest!
Pulled from a hoarding situation and understandably overwhelmed, Meowy Dearest arrived wary but watchful. With calm voices and a gentle approach, she'll tolerate brief petting and is starting to relax on her perch. She's an independent, curious girl who'll do best with a patient person willing to let trust grow at her pace.

My Ideal Home
An experienced, low-traffic home that understands shy cats. Start her in a quiet "decompression" room with hiding spots and vertical perches; keep interactions short and choice-based, and pair your presence with tasty treats. Coming from a hoarding environment, predictable routines will help her feel safe and blossom over time.

Good with Kids?
Best with adults only or older, cat-savvy teens who can move slowly and respect her boundaries.

Good with Other Pets?
History with pets is unknown. A very calm resident cat may help model confidence if introductions are extra slow, but she could also thrive as a solo cat while she settles in.

A volunteer writes: Like her namesake, Mermaidia is a sight to behold: In lieu of flashy iridescent scales is a beautiful merle coat and eyes that sparkle in the sun. But Mermaidia's vibe is anything but flashy. She's a quiet, timid girl who's sometimes hesitant to leave the safety of the crate she's called home since arriving at the shelter - she often needs some gentle coaxing and baby talk. Once she hits the pavement, though, she's happy to walk nicely alongside us and snack on all the treats we have to offer, and she was even lucky enough to go on a Boroughbreak her first week at the shelter. During her outing, this smart girl demonstrated she knew the commands for "sit," "paw," and "down," and was a model citizen. (Her Boroughbreakers described her as sweet, calm, and adorable, and we can't think of three more accurate adjectives.) Mermaidia was dropped off by an anonymous person at a police station in Brooklyn, and she's estimated to be just a little over a year old. Miia came to the shelter with Miia 256742 after their family experienced housing insecurity. This sweet, affectionate girl is equal parts cuddle bug and couch potato, happiest when she's relaxing near her favorite people or handing out kisses to everyone she loves.

My Ideal Home
Miia is looking for a calm home that will appreciate her gentle, easygoing personality while also keeping her mind engaged with walks, enrichment toys, and positive reinforcement training. She enjoys spending time with her family, loves car rides and bath time, and already knows cues like "sit," "stay," and "paw."

Good with Other Pets?
Miia has lived successfully with another dog and is friendly with familiar canine companions. She can be shy around unfamiliar dogs and is uncomfortable with off-leash greetings, so slow introductions are important. Because she can be reactive to unfamiliar dogs and small animals, dog parks are not recommended.

Good with Kids?
A home without young children is recommended. Miia can become protective of high-value items like toys and prefers to enjoy them without interruption, so an older household that can respect her space will help set her up for success.

Things to Know
Miia is a loving, low-energy companion who enjoys following her people from room to room before settling in for a cozy nap. She can be anxious when left alone and prefers gentle handling, especially around her paws, which can sometimes be uncomfortable. She also likes to keep her favorite toys to herself, so teaching fun trade games and giving her space with treasured items will help her succeed. With patience, consistency, and lots of love, Miia will reward her new family with endless affection, quiet companionship, and plenty of sweet kisses. A volunteer writes: Meet momma Miia! I can't decide if it's more fun to cuddle with her or watch her fetch. Round in all the right places, surprisingly quick on her feet! When I call, she trots over with a joyful jiggle, tail wagging, and leans into cuddles. Her signature move is crawling into a hug when you put out your hand asking for paw. This smart girl gets praise from the canine behavior team for her exemplary work on "leave it" and engaging with positive reinforcement training. Out for a walk, she is chill on a leash and non-reactive, and has been housebroken with regular walks. Miia came to us with her sister, Myyha (ID 256743), when their guardian experienced housing insecurity. She had lived with older kids and dogs, and was described as friendly with familiar dogs, though at times shy with unfamiliar ones. In a shelter dog intro, she approached with a loose, neutral body, and disengaged. She's reported to love bath time and water, car tides, know multiple cues, and shower her people with affection and kisses. Meet Milky Way!
Milky Way was found walking alone on the street. She is a sensitive, gentle girl who is trying her best in a very new environment. She shows small but meaningful moments of trust with people she begins to know. With calm handling and patience, she can settle and seek comfort from her handler.

My Ideal Home
Milky Way would do best in a quiet, adult-only home with experience or willingness to work with fearful dogs. She will need a patient adopter who allows her to adjust at her own pace without pressure.

Good with Other Pets?
Milky Way has shown mixed responses to other dogs and can become tense in close or high-energy interactions. Careful, structured introductions and ongoing management would be important in a home with other animals.

Good with Kids?
Milky Way is recommended for a home without children under 13 due to her fearful and sensitive nature. She will do best in a calm, low-stimulation environment.

Things to Know
Milky Way walks nicely on leash but may freeze or hesitate in unfamiliar environments. She is very sensitive to handling and does best with slow introductions and gentle encouragement. With time and consistency, she shows the ability to relax and connect with her person.

Fun Fact
Milky Way may start out a little starry-eyed and unsure, but once she trusts you, she shines brightly!🌌 Milky Way is enrolled in our Shelter Scholar program and is making wonderful progress on her leash manners. Encounters with other dogs or unexpected distractions can be overwhelming for her during walks, but through her training she is learning to settle, refocus, and trust her handler. Milo was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him. He is a sweet, social older gentleman who enjoys being around people and is known for his affectionate, easygoing nature once he is comfortable in a home environment. He can be vocal and expressive, but he is very people-oriented and enjoys companionship.

My Ideal Home
Milo would do best in a calm and loving home that can match his lower energy level and appreciate his affectionate, homebody personality. He enjoys being close to his people and thrives with routine, gentle structure, and continued support for his mild anxiety when left alone.

Good with Other Pets?
Milo is friendly with familiar dogs but may react to unfamiliar dogs on leash. He should be monitored around other animals and would do best with controlled introductions.

Good with Kids?
Due to his reactivity toward unfamiliar animals and need for a calm environment, Milo is recommended for a home without children under 13.

Things to Know
Milo is a low-energy, affectionate companion who enjoys relaxing at home, following his people around, and spending most of his day lounging. He is housetrained, enjoys car rides, and has experience with grooming and basic cues like sit and stay. He can be anxious when left alone and may bark or become vocal, so continued support around separation anxiety will be important. He walks with only mild pulling and is otherwise tolerant of handling and daily care. With consistency and reassurance, Milo shines as a loyal, loving companion who enjoys the simple comforts of home life.

Fun Fact
Milo's favorite things include dressing up for photos, celebrating birthdays, and lounging like the perfect little couch companion with his people nearby. A volunteer writes: The first time I meet Milo I am smitten by the way his little ears take flight on our walk, flapping in the breeze, as he shows off his loose leash skills. As he meanders toward me he sends delicate little yips into the air followed by a full on serenade of glorious howls, worthy, in my opinion of a Metropolitan Opera soloist. This is not Milo's first time in our shelter unfortunately. He was surrendered once before due to a domestic violence situation and then again due to health issues in his family. He is reported to have done well with the children and small dog in his previous home and is a "playful yet lazy couch potato" who "loves chicken". He has also spent some time in foster where it was said he "was friends with all the doormen". Medically, he has a mass which will need to be checked out. Miu Miu is on the At Risk list due to behavior. She is not thriving in the care center and continues to display challenging behavior during interactions. In addition to playtime, this cat would also benefit from mental exercise from activities such as puzzle toys/games, lick mats, or clicker training. It is in his/her best interest to move out of the kennel environment and into a stable home as quickly as possible. She would do best in a home with adopters who are willing to give her plenty of time and space to adjust, and who have experience with feline body language, overstimulation, rough play, and who have the time to invest in managing these behaviors on a consistent basis to avoid further bite/scratch incidents.

He's low-key suspicious of the TV, and while he's not especially food motivated, he'll gladly accept a Churu as a peace offering. Morty loves playing hide and seek, chasing wand and string toys, zooming through his tunnel, and occasionally batting at your feet from beneath the couch. He isn't needy, but he is affectionate once you earn his trust. He'll wander out to check on you, meow politely for back/butt scratches, and sometimes curl up next to you or in your lap. When he's really comfortable, he'll dramatically flop over for pets, roll around showing his belly, and gently paw at you if you stop petting him too soon. He purrs loudly and even drools a little when he's extra happy. He'll check on you in the bathroom to make sure you're okay, and somehow always needs attention the second you're on a meeting. He tolerates being picked up (while looking mildly confused), then may casually scamper off once you put him down. Laid back, independent, sweet, and a little goofy - Morty just does things on his own time, and it makes it special when he chooses you. 🐾

Morty tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. He may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to his new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, he may not be a great fit for young children.

Meet Morty!
Morty came to ACC after living with adults in a home environment. He is a shy, timid cat who prefers to take things slowly, especially in new surroundings. In the shelter, Morty can appear cautious or stressed at first, but with gentle handling and time, he shows tolerance for petting and curiosity about his caregivers. He enjoys calm interactions and prefers affection on his own terms.

My Ideal Home
Morty would thrive in a quiet, low-traffic home with experienced cat parents who understand shy or sensitive cats. He needs time to acclimate, patience, and a predictable routine. Allowing him space to settle in, approach voluntarily, and build trust gradually will help him feel secure and confident.

Good with Kids?
No young children. ACC recommends Morty be placed in a home without children under 5, as he needs extra time to warm up and may become stressed in busy or unpredictable environments.

Mozz came to ACC after his owner passed away, and while his past is unknown, he's shown himself to be a social, playful, and people-oriented dog who enjoys attention and treats. He's a happy greeter who leans into interactions and is eager to engage with handlers.

My Ideal Home
Mozz would do well in an active, structured home that can continue teaching him polite manners and impulse control in a positive, consistent way. He thrives with engagement, training, and clear boundaries, especially around excitement and food rewards.

Good with Other Pets?
Mozz ignores other dogs in leash observations. Slow and careful introductions with resident pets are always recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to his mouthiness and high arousal when taking treats, Mozz is recommended for a home without young children under 5. He may be open to older, respectful children after a meet.

Things to Know
Mozz is an affectionate, playful dog who gets very excited during interaction and can jump up frequently when seeking attention or treats. He takes treats with a very hard mouth at times, so continued positive reinforcement training around impulse control and gentle mouth behavior is important. He is otherwise tolerant of handling, enjoys engagement, and walks nicely on leash with only mild pulling. With consistency and structure, Mozz has strong potential to channel his enthusiasm into great manners and reliable behavior.

My Ideal Home
Mr. Speckles would do best in a calm, quiet home with someone who understands that confidence takes time. He will need slow introductions to new people and places, along with plenty of patience, routine, and positive reinforcement to help him feel secure. A peaceful environment where he can decompress and learn that he is safe will help him shine.

Good with Other Pets?
Mr. Speckles has not shown reactivity toward other dogs while in our care, but his history with other animals is unknown. Slow and thoughtful introductions are recommended for any resident pets.

Good with Kids?
Due to his fearful nature and need for a slow approach, Mr. Speckles would do best in an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Mr. Speckles is a shy and sensitive pup who may need extra time before he feels comfortable in a new environment. He appreciates gentle interactions and should always be allowed to approach people and new experiences at his own pace. Once he feels safe, his sweet personality can begin to shine. If you have a quiet home and a big heart for a dog who needs a little extra patience, Mr. Speckles may be the perfect companion for you. Myyha came to the shelter with Mia 256742 after their family experienced housing insecurity. This social, affectionate girl is full of personality and loves being part of whatever her people are doing. Whether she's joining you for a car ride, splashing around in the water, or soaking up cuddles, Myyha is happiest by your side.

My Ideal Home
Myyha is looking for an active home that can keep up with her playful energy. She'll enjoy daily walks, enrichment activities, and positive reinforcement training to help channel her enthusiasm. She's very food motivated, knows cues like "sit," "stay," and "paw," and loves meeting new people, making her a fun companion to continue learning with.

Good with Other Pets?
Myyha has lived successfully with another dog and enjoys familiar canine friends. She can be uncertain around unfamiliar dogs, so slow introductions are recommended, and dog parks are not the right fit for her. She should also live in a home without cats or other small animals, as she has a history of chasing them on walks.

Good with Kids?
An adult-only home is recommended. Myyha can become protective of high-value toys and prefers to enjoy them without interruption, so a home that can respect her space will help her feel comfortable and successful.

One Bunzy is a 3-year-old long stay pup who came in as a stray and is now waiting patiently for her chance at a forever home. She is a longstay and her adoption fee has been reduced!

Personality
One Bunzy is a sweet, friendly, and affectionate girl who truly enjoys being close to people. Her foster describes her as calm, loving, and very people oriented, often happily resting her head on your lap for attention and cuddles. She is gentle in her interactions and seems to enjoy forming quiet, steady bonds with those she trusts.

She is also smart and eager to please, with a natural willingness to learn. Her foster notes she seems easy to train and responsive to positive attention, especially when she feels safe and included.

Out and About
One Bunzy is an easy leash walker with no pulling and no reactivity toward people or other dogs. She moves calmly through her environment and tends to stay close to her handler. She enjoys steady, relaxed walks and benefits from continued positive experiences outside the home.

Social Behavior
In the shelter, One Bunzy is highly social and approaches handlers readily with a soft body and gentle wagging tail. She accepts both soft and more active handling and remains neutral and relaxed during interaction. She enjoys being near people and shows a calm, steady interest in connection.

In a dog interaction on 09/23/25, One Bunzy showed a soft body and wagging tail but chose not to approach the gate, suggesting a polite and observational style when meeting other dogs.

Home Life
One Bunzy will thrive in a home that can offer love, consistency, and gentle structure. She enjoys being part of daily life, whether that means going for walks or simply relaxing at home beside her person. She will benefit from positive outlets for her energy, such as toys and enrichment activities, even though she is not highly toy motivated right now. Bunzy is a Level 1 dog, meaning she is suitable for the majority of households.

Things to Know
One Bunzy has medical needs that staff will discuss with adopters. She enjoys social interaction, but her history with other animals and children is unknown, so slow introductions will be important.

Fun Fact
One Bunzy is kind of dog who doesn't ask for much, just a little love, a soft place to rest her head, and someone to walk through life with by her side. 🐾

My foster writes: If you are looking for a loyal, people-loving shadow, meet Bunzy! She is an incredibly sweet, even-tempered girl who absolutely adores human company. Bunzy is the ultimate "velcro puppy"her favorite place in the world is right next to you (or literally on you!). Whether she's squeezing herself into your office chair to "help" you work, or adjusting her sleeping position at night to make sure her body is glued right next to your head, Bunzy just wants to be close. Oreo Cookie was surrendered when her owner could no longer care for her and is ready to start a new chapter with a loving family. She is an affectionate girl who enjoys leaning in for pets, spending time with her people, and exploring the world by your side. With a little patience and guidance, Oreo Cookie is sure to be one sweet companion.

My Ideal Home
Oreo Cookie would thrive in a patient home that can provide a consistent routine, positive reinforcement training, and plenty of enrichment. Daily walks, puzzle toys, and fun training sessions will help keep both her mind and body busy. She may need a little extra support as she adjusts to being left alone, but with time and reassurance, she'll continue building confidence.

Good with Other Pets?
Oreo Cookie previously lived with a small dog and was described as friendly with familiar canine companions. She can be uncomfortable around unfamiliar dogs while on leash, so slow introductions and continued positive reinforcement training will help her succeed. Dog parks are not recommended, as she is happiest meeting dogs in calmer, more controlled settings.

Good with Kids?
Because Oreo Cookie can be sensitive in new situations and is still building confidence, a home without very young children is recommended. Older children who understand how to respect her space may be a great fit.

Things to Know
Oreo Cookie loves attention and happily leans in for affection, though she may jump up when she's excited to say hello. She can be startled by unfamiliar situations and may need slow introductions to new experiences, but she responds well to gentle, reward based training. With a little patience and a lot of love, this sweet cookie is ready to become the best part of someone's day. Due to his enthusiastic greetings and occasional mouthiness when excited, ACC recommends a home with no young children.

Fun Fact

Whether he's making new friends, showing off his playful side, or curling up for a well-earned nap, he's happiest when he's with his favorite people. Overall Health

Otis has a quiet, observant personality and enjoys gentle head rubs once he feels safe. He gives little "thank you tail lifts" as he warms up, and his sweet, thoughtful nature shines through during calm one-on-one interactions. Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home!

Meet Pinto Bean!
Pinto Bean was found tied to a bench in a park and has been showing us ever since that she's got a big heart and plenty of energy to match. She is social, people-oriented, and happiest when she has someone to engage with. With a little guidance, she really starts to shine.

Personality
Pinto Bean is a lively, affectionate girl who enjoys attention and connection. She may bounce between exploring and checking in with her person, especially when she's feeling excited. Once she settles, she enjoys affection and can be very sweet and engaging one-on-one.

My Ideal Home
Pinto Bean would do best in an adult-only home that can match her energy and provide structure. She's a great fit for someone who enjoys an active, interactive companion.

Good with Other Pets?
Pinto Bean has shown neutral, appropriate greetings with other dogs and is able to disengage and re-approach calmly. With thoughtful introductions, she may enjoy polite canine companions.

Good with Kids?
Pinto Bean is recommended for an adult-only home due to her high energy and excitement level.

Things to Know
Pinto Bean is strong on leash and will benefit from continued leash training and structure. She is very responsive training, especially when treats are involved.

Fun Fact
Pinto Bean is always ready to "refry" your expectations of a shelter dog with her big personality and even bigger heart. She's got the kind of energy that makes every day a little more seasoned.

Months","type":"Dog","species":"Dog","link":"https://nycacc.app/browse/256903","gender":"Male","summaryHtml":"Meet Pryce!
Pryce was surrendered when his owner could no longer care for him. His former family describes him as social, affectionate, playful, and very active. Whether he's cuddling on the couch, rolling around in the grass, or joining you for a car ride, Pryce is happiest when he's spending time with his people.

My Ideal Home
Pryce is looking for an active, adult only home that can keep up with his playful personality while helping him learn to settle. He'll thrive with plenty of daily exercise, enrichment, and positive reinforcement training. He already knows cues like sit, stop, shake, lay down, and "stop barking," and loves healthy treats like carrots and cucumbers.

Good with Other Pets?
Pryce previously lived with both a small and a medium sized dog. According to his former owner, he is playful and outgoing with familiar dogs and initially shy around unfamiliar ones. At the care center, he greeted another dog politely through a barrier with loose, friendly body language after warming up, so slow introductions to resident dogs are recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to his high arousal level, jumping, and mouthy behavior, ACC recommends an adult only home for Pryce.

Things to Know
Pryce is a high energy dog who will need regular physical exercise and mental enrichment to help him thrive. With structure, patience, and force-free training, Pryce has all the ingredients to become an incredible companion for an active family.

Fun Fact
Pryce loves playing in the grass, enjoys car rides, and would never turn down his favorite snacks: crunchy carrots and cucumbers. A volunteer wrtes: Pryce is just a special boy. He is only 9 months old and an interesting mix of breeds! He reminds us of a shar pei with his tiny corn chip ears and curly tail, but he is thinner and less fluffy. He is reported to be a shar pei doberman mix! Pryce's ultimate special feature is his toes! He has many extra! His back feet look like he has 2 extras toes per foot! Pryce is also just a wonderful personality. He is sweet, social, playful and I am truly shocked he wasn't adopted immediately. Pryce came to us when his owner was homeless. He had been living with his owner in a car, but ultimately that was not sustainable. He had spent time around strangers and children and was friendly and gentle. He spent time with a small and medium dog, both of which he was outgoing and playful with. He can be shy around novel dogs. At the shelter he greeted a dog with a soft neutral, and wiggly frame. He enjoys car rides, knows basic cues, and he likes to cuddle and play. He is a healthy boy and his favorite snacks are carrots and cucumbers! Years","type":"Dog","species":"Dog","link":"https://nycacc.app/browse/251205","gender":"Male","summaryHtml":"Meet Quinn!
Quinn was found abandoned on the street and has shown himself to be a social, energetic, and affectionate young dog who loves play, enrichment, and spending time with people. He is especially people-oriented and quickly bonds with handlers, often greeting them with enthusiasm and playful behavior.

My Ideal Home
Quinn would do best in an active, structured home that helps him channel his energy into positive outlets such as training, enrichment, and exercise. He benefits from consistency, patience, and continued work on impulse control, confidence building, and calm handling.

Good with Other Pets?
Quinn has shown interest in other dogs during introductions and is generally social, but interactions should always be supervised and carefully managed to ensure comfort for all dogs involved.

Good with Kids?
Due to his exuberance, impulse control needs, and handling sensitivity, Quinn is recommended for an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Quinn is a playful and affectionate dog who loves toys, attention, and interactive time with people. He can be easily spooked by loud noises and may become overly excited during handling or play, so continued positive reinforcement training is important. He is working on skills like settling on a mat and polite exchange, and he responds very well to food motivation and structure. He is a social and engaged walker, though he can be strong on leash at times. With consistency and support, Quinn continues to grow more confident and focused each day.

Volunteer Note
A volunteer writes: As I sit with Quinn in the play yard, watching him retrieve balls or joyously tossing a soft toy into the air for himself, I marvel at how trusting and open he remains after 70 days in confinement. All I can offer is a 15-minute walk, Pupperoni and cuddles, yet he greets me like I'm his BFF. When I call out to him, he runs to me like I'm a long-lost friend, then hops into my lap, happily accepting pets. This young, energetic boy loves carefree playtime, but is also food motivated, which is great for learning. He is similarly noted by the shelter's canine behavior team to be social (and even playbowing to them!) & engage with enrichment as he works on impulse control, a skill that would be understandably easier for an adolescent to develop in a consistent home environment. Bonus: he comes pre-housebroken! In shelter assessments, he's been found to ignore dogs on walks, and take positive interest in another dog during a supervised introduction. Quinn is enrolled in our Shelter Scholar program and is putting in great work each and every day. He is developing two important skills, polite exchange and relaxing on a mat, both of which are helping him become a more grounded and easygoing companion. With positive reinforcement guiding the way, Quinn is growing more confident and composed with every training session.

Fun Fact
Quinn doesn't just play fetch, he also invents his own games, turning every toy into an opportunity for fun and connection. My previous foster writes: Ramona is five years old and 15lbs. Her coat is a silky dark grey and her eyes shift orange to green. She may at first dodge or hide but once she feels at home, all humans are welcome visitors to her queendom. Ramona will greet you by running towards you and rubbing against your legs, ask to bonk her head against yours, then flop at your feet and stretch out to show her belly. She loves belly pets! Ramona is a large cat, and some large cats need help with grooming. Ramona can clean herself after using the litter box but she needs help on her back. She adores brush time and asks for help grooming after her meals. Ramona is regal. She wears a dark grey coat and has tiny ivory fangs. Ramona wants churu for dinner and is slow to eat most other wet foods even with churu mixed in. Ramona is curious and wants to be involved, but she is not exactly food motivated. She enjoys sitting and dozing quite near her person. She is mildly interested in the house and considers the bedroom her HQ between short explorations. Ramona enjoys string toys, feathered balls, and springs. She plays by herself and asks to play an equal amount.

What my friends at ACC say about me:

Ramona tolerates attention and petting but appears fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent, and may need time to warm up to her new home. We recommend this cat go to a home with experienced cat parents. Due to the behavior shown, she may not be a great fit for young children.

My Ideal Home
Rollie would do best in a calm, quiet home that can give her time to feel safe and build confidence. She enjoys having space to hop, zoom, and explore, and then happily settles in for pets once she feels comfortable. Good with Kids?
Rollie may do well with older, respectful children who understand that rabbits are prey animals and don't always like to be handled. A quieter household would be ideal for her sensitive nature.

Good with Other Pets?
Rollie has shown no signs of aggression and may be a good candidate for bonding with another calm rabbit with proper introductions. Her gentle personality suggests she could enjoy a companion once she's settled.

Overall Health
Rollie is healthy overall and has been treated preventatively for parasites. She has maintained a good appetite and normal activity levels in care, with no ongoing medical concerns noted at this time.

Behavior Determination
Level 1 - Rollie is a gentle rabbit suitable for adopters of any experience level who can provide a calm environment, patience, and appropriate rabbit enrichment.

Ronnie pulls moderately on the leash and is nonreactive to humans and dogs on walks.

Ronnie has been assessed as a Level 2 dog. She would love to meet an adopter that will allow her to decompress at her own pace. With patience and understanding, Ronnie would make a very special companion!

Salem may have had a rocky start after being found abandoned near a police precinct, but this sweet boy is ready to turn the page and find a loving home. While he can be a little shy when meeting new people, Salem has shown that he has a gentle heart and enjoys affection once he feels comfortable. With a little patience and a lot of love, this sweet pup is ready to cast a spell on his forever family.

My Ideal Home
Salem would do best with a patient adopter who understands that confidence takes time to grow. A calm, predictable environment and slow introductions will help him feel safe as he adjusts to his new surroundings. He will thrive with someone who can help him build confidence through positive reinforcement, enrichment, and plenty of encouragement.

Good with Other Pets?
Salem's history with other animals is unknown. During his time at the shelter, he has shown some uncertainty around unfamiliar dogs, so slow and controlled introductions would be the best way to help him feel comfortable. A home without dog parks is recommended so Salem can continue building positive experiences at his own pace.

Good with Kids?
Due to Salem's shy nature and need for gentle interactions, he would do best in a home with adults or older children who can respect his boundaries and give him time to warm up.

Things to Know
Salem is a gentle soul who enjoys quiet moments and taking life one paw at a time. He walks nicely on leash, enjoys treats, and will happily lean in for pets once he feels comfortable. Salem can become anxious in new situations, so a patient adopter who can help him feel safe will be the key to helping this sweet boy blossom. If you're looking for a loyal companion who just needs a little time to let his true colors shine, Salem might be your perfect match! Pre-Screener Form

Sheba came inot the care cneter as an owner surrender due to having too many animals in the home. Her previously owner's favorite thing about her is how sweet, gentle, and affectionate she is. She loves being close to her people. She has a calm personality, enjoys relaxing in sunny spots or cozy blankets, and is very loyal. She is well-behaved in the home, loves attention, and has a loving nature that makes her a wonderful companion. Sheba enjoys going for walks, relaxing outdoors in the sun, cuddling with her family, and taking naps on soft blankets. Sheba has not acclimated well to the kennel environment and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home. A volunteer writes: It is especially heartbreaking to see a dog once living a comfortable life in a loving home struggle to get comfortable in a shelter environment. Sheba was surrendered due to her previous guardian having too many animals in the home. She lived with three other dogs, two adults, and one child. Their favorite thing about her was how sweet, gentle, and affectionate she is - and I can see all of those attributes shine through when I meet her, despite being a little uncertain about this new place she now calls home. Hello! I have ringworm, a treatable fungal infection of the skin that can be itchy but otherwise harmless in minor cases like mine. I require a course of Itraconazole, an antifungal medication that is taken by mouth every day for a few weeks. Ringworm can be transmissible to humans and other animals, so it's important to keep me separate from other pets in the home, wash hands after playing with me, and perhaps have a specific set of clothes to wear when interacting with me. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. It's also a good idea to make sure fabrics in the room I'm housed in are washed frequently - who knew adopting a kitty with ringworm would be a great way to help you stay on top of your household cleaning too?

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!

I am playful and cute!
