If you're looking for a loyal member of your pride, I'm your guy. When I venture beyond Pride Rock, I enjoy greeting humans with a friendly sniff and saving my best kisses for my favorite people. I'm more Rafiki than wildebeest stampede-I prefer calm, peaceful surroundings so I can sleep all day. Sometimes, when I see other dogs that want to play with me, I feel compelled to give them my best lion impression so they know I'd love to play. What can I say? A future king has to make his presence known! My foster writes: Hi, I'm Simba, and my favorite place in the world is being by your side. My dream job is a full-time work-from-home coworker, and I take my duties very seriously: napping next to your desk, snuggling next to you on the couch, and proudly squeaking my toys during breaks. When we're out and about, I love sniffing humans and licking my favorite ones. I'm more of a calm-vibes kind of guy and would love a quieter home (as I am still learning that many humans can live on apartment floors). Sometimes I feel that other dogs on walks want to hear my voice and see me jump so they know I want to play with them.Humans say I am a smarty-paws as I'm crate-trained, already know tricks (sit, down, and paw), and think that bathrooms belong outside. Now all I need is my forever humans. Could that be you? Searching for a loyal sidekick who never misses a bathroom trip? This sweet boy is happiest being near you and would excel in his dream career as a full-time work-from-home coworker. He is always down to nap next to your desk, snuggle next to you on the couch, or chew on his squeaky toys. Outside, he's friendly with people and incredibly attentive. He thrives in calm. quieter surroundings without too much hustle and bustle and is looking for walks in low dog areas. Simba is also a total smarty-paws, crate-trained and has mastered "sit," "down," and "paw." If you're ready to meet a gentle soul, Simba's your guy!

What my friends at ACC say about me:

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

I love getting pets and - you guessed it - snuggles!

I would do best in a home without very tiny humans, although I could be open to older human children once I meet them.

I am excitable and energetic! I will need positive outlets for my energy!

A volunteer writes: I spent some time with Mr. Slips today, and now that he's more adjusted to the Care Center, he seems like a totally different cat than his earlier notes state: I found him to be playful, gentle, and a lover of any and all human interaction. This handsome youngster waited patiently for me to approach his kennel, and when I did he greeted me with some hearty meows and an invitation to bat around a feather toy. He took a break to munch some chow, then lay down on his side and rolled around to reveal his belly, a sign of trust. Slips really is a fan of humans, and the perfect new pet parent for him is someone who keeps a pile of toys on hand and gives him one-on-one time. Snickers arrived at Queens ACC as a stray in rough condition, but he's been steadily healing and showing more of his gentle personality each day. Despite limited history, staff have already seen a sweet, soft-natured boy who is tolerant, calm, and beginning to open up as he recovers.

My Ideal Home
Snickers would do best in a patient, low-pressure home that can give him time to fully recover and settle in. He benefits from gentle routines, calm environments, and positive reinforcement as he continues building confidence. As he heals, he will likely thrive with quiet structure and steady encouragement.

Good with Other Pets?
Snickers' history with other animals is unknown, so slow introductions are recommended if there are resident pets.

Good with Kids?
Due to his fearful presentation and need for a calm environment, ACC recommends a home without young children under 5.

Things to Know
Snickers is a gentle, observant dog who can be a bit reserved at first, sometimes choosing to move away from interaction until he feels comfortable. Once leashed, he walks calmly at a steady pace and may pause or resist briefly but responds well to treats and reassurance. He tolerates handling and has shown soft, friendly body language such as tail wagging and relaxed behavior during care. As he continues to heal medically, his full personality is still emerging, but he already shows strong potential to become a loving companion with time and patience.

Fun Fact
Even while recovering, Snickers has been spotted quietly wagging his tail and gently leaning into attention-he's a soft-hearted boy who's just getting started on his second chance.

This animal has a little extra support from Bond Vet! Adopt this cutie and receive $1000 in your Bond Vet account to get their vet care started on the right foot.

Spice has spent nearly 25% of his life in the shelter after being brought in stray/abandoned. He is such a sweet boy who has persevered despite his long journey. His demeanor is that of a puppy younger than his stated two years as is typical of puppies who find themselves living the shelter life. Despite these obstacles, he possesses a certain stoicism - as if his past has rendered him simply grateful for love and support. In foster, he is working very well on his puppy manners. Spice makes such a loyal companion; if you are looking for an amazing, potty-trained, funny dude - he is ready for his forever home. House Broken?...Yes. Crate Trained?...Yes. Toy and/or Resource Guarding?...No. Personality & Energy Level Spice is goofy, playful and yet very smart. He is affectionate, has emotional intelligence and plays with a moderate energy level. Belly rub requests are his standard and he loves to cuddle on the couch. He does get a cute case of the zoomies from time to time. Spice can be slightly fearful/skittish as he acclimates to his new environment. Supporting puppy growth and development with enrichment will serve Spice well! Spice is wonderful in the car; he loves taking in the world through a window! Social Skills: Kids & Dogs It is unknown if Spice lived with children. All introductions should be careful and thoughtful. He has shown good demeanor with elementary aged children who had previous dog experience and moved slowly with him. Spice is "mouthy" defined as: a natural way for puppies to explore their environment and relieve teething pain. As an Adult dog, referred to as "jumpy/mouthy," this usually stems from having excess energy, never learning appropriate play boundaries as a new puppy, and/or excessive stress (i.e. abandonment and shelter life). This is addressed with a consistent environment - daily walks, affection and no-fear training. With dogs, Spice can be reactive particularly in crowded, busy environments. Spice was easily redirected with command of his short leash and verbal commands like "no Spice, let's go" and/or "leave it". In foster, he did very well in suburban environments. He walks well on his leash, with mild pulling. Home Time & Separation Spice is housebroken, crate trained and quiet. He shows some signs of separation anxiety (laying at the front door, whimpering), but with time, he grows more trusting in longer durations alone. Like most puppies, he does best being with his human(s). While he is training on being home alone, crating is recommended. He has shown no signs of destructive behavior in foster, but he is very smart and knows how to stand to attempt to open doors. He chooses the couch or his crate as a peaceful spot to nap and he sleeps peacefully through the night from his semi-covered his crate - so long as he can see out. Gentle bath time was good (doesn't love the dryer but what pup does!). He was also non-reactive to the washer/dryer or vacuum! Diet, Health, Exercise & Wellness Spice's diet is currently GI focused. He is treat driven but won't hesitate to spit out something he doesn't like! He loves water (& really appreciates his water bottle on outdoor outings on hot days)! Spice loves going on walks however he is being assessed for a healing hind leg(s) so walks (after he goes potty) are limited to 10-15 minutes and stairs avoided - current information can be discussed with his ACC team. Since I'm a long stay pup, my adoption fee has been reduced! Visit me today to find out my favorite treats and how you can take me home! Meet Spice!
This lively, affectionate boy is full of personality and love, and he's ready for a home that can keep up with him and help him feel secure.

My Ideal Home
Spice would do best in an active, adult-only home that can give him plenty of exercise, structure, and companionship. He prefers not to be alone for long and thrives when he has his people nearby.

Good with Other Pets?
Spice's interactions with other dogs have been mixed and can be a bit overwhelming for him. He would do best with slow, structured introductions or as the only pet while he continues to build confidence.

Good with Kids?
No children under 13, as Spice can become overexcited and benefits from an adult-only home.

Things to Know
Spice is a high-energy, affectionate dog who loves attention and will happily jump in for pets, playtime, or even a cuddle in your lap. He can get a little overexcited at times and will benefit from continued training to build calm behaviors and impulse control. He prefers company and may struggle when left alone for long periods, so enrichment, routine, and companionship are key. He also enjoys his toys and does best with positive "trade" games to keep things fun and safe.

Stack was found tied up in front of a precinct with another dog. He's an independent guy who is still learning that the world and new people are safe, and he's looking for a calm, patient home to help him come out of his shell.

My Ideal Home
Stack would love a quiet, adult only home where he can settle in at his own pace. He enjoys getting out for walks and sniffing around, and he'll do best with a family that gives him time, structure, and lots of positive reinforcement as he builds confidence. Once he feels comfortable, his gentle, curious side starts to shine.

Good with Other Pets?
Stack showed brief, polite interest in another dog at the care center, but became tense during the interaction and was moved away for his comfort. His history with other animals is unknown, so any introductions to resident dogs should be slow and thoughtful. He may be happiest as the only pet in the home.

Good with Kids?
Due to his fearfulness and sensitivity in new situations, Stack is recommended for an adult-only home at this time.

Things to Know
Stack is a thoughtful, observant dog who can be a bit anxious in new environments and prefers to take things at his own pace. He is generally tolerant of handling but appreciates gentle, low-pressure interactions and the freedom to step away when he needs space. With patience, consistency, and positive reinforcement, Stack has a great foundation to grow into a trusting and loyal companion.

Fun Fact
Stack has a soft, curious side that comes out more each day. Once he feels safe, he enjoys exploring and quietly taking in the world around him. My foster parents love that I am a curious and playful kitty, yet also a calm companion who enjoys being near you. I thrive in a peaceful environment because I can be a bit nervous and easily startled, but I've been growing more confident every day. The presence of another cat at home has been really soothing for me and reassuring of safety. Having him around has been an important boost of my trust in humans. I get along very well with my resident cat brother, I like to follow his lead and see the world the way he shows it to me. I constantly seek to play and hang out with him. I also love chasing toys, playing with feather wands, racing for my favorite treats, and I am an exceptional fly's hunter. Most of the time, I am a silent boy, but I can get vocal if I'm worried. Sometimes, I also vocalize when I get excited to see my cat brother or when I want some pets, because yes, I ask for them. I am a sweet and affectionate kitty, always ready to melt into your hands. I don't mind you rubbing all of my body, but my favorites are scratches on my chin, cheeks, and the base of my tail. I can also allow belly rubs, which turns me into a cuddling baby. I especially love when people talk to me softly, it makes me feel safe, loved, and cherished. I'm still a little unsure about kisses and not to fond of being carried on hands, but I'm slowly learning to tolerate it. And I have even allowed my nails to be clipped three times already! I am a master at finding cozy, hidden spots for naps during the day, and if I hear something fun happening, I'll want to be included and will run to join in immediately. But don't get me wrong, I also love to nap on the bed near you while you watch TV. I appreciate your patience in getting to know me since I need time to trust people. With time, my foster parents believe I'll grow into a big cuddler. If you're seeking the ideal mix of curiosity, playfulness, quietness, and independent companionship, I hope to find a loving forever home with you.

Starlight Twilight tolerates some attention and petting but may be fearful or stressed in the shelter, and may be intimidated by small children. Due to the behaviors seen in the care center, we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced, adult only home.

Sunflower Seeds arrived at the care center after being brought in by NYPD when she was found unattended at a precinct, and from the moment she arrived she's shown a friendly, social personality. This happy girl is full of life, curiosity, and enthusiasm for the world around her.

My Ideal Home
Sunflower Seeds would thrive in an active home that enjoys engaging, hands-on time with their dog. She's a bright, energetic girl who will benefit from structure, routine, and ongoing training to help her channel her excitement into positive behaviors. She loves treats and will happily work for them, making her a great candidate for reward-based learning.

Good with Other Pets?
Her history with other animals is unknown, so slow and thoughtful introductions to any resident pets are recommended.

Good with Kids?
It is unknown if Sunflower Seeds has lived with children previously, so careful introductions are recommended depending on the household.

Things to Know
Sunflower Seeds is a lively, social dog who can be very exuberant when meeting people and may jump up frequently due to her enthusiasm. On leash, she can pull moderately toward places she wants to explore, but she is otherwise friendly and responsive. In the care center, she's shown a playful, outgoing personality, enjoys interacting with handlers, and already knows cues like sit and paw. With consistent positive reinforcement training, she'll continue to blossom into a well-mannered companion.

Fun Fact
On her BoroughBreak, Sunflower Seeds explored Central Park, relaxed in the Conservatory Garden, and even enjoyed a picnic, proving she's just as sweet and fun as her name suggests. When the kennel door is opened, she tenses slightly, remaining in her position on top of the den. Initially when petting is attempted, Suzie backs away to avoid contact. The assessor softly speaks to her and offers a squeeze up treat, and she sniffs the air before quickly coming forward to eat it. Suzie is tolerant of all petting while she eats, not engaging and tail held low. She is unable to be coaxed down from the top of the den, so pickup is unable to be attempted. She is tolerant of light upward pressure applied to her sides and under her chest, remaining slightly tense but without further issue.

Suzie tolerates attention and petting but appears to be moderately fearful or stressed in the shelter. She may be a little more independent and may need time to warm up to her new home. Giving me lyme sulfur dip baths a couple of times per week can also help to minimize risk of spreading. He was very calm when picked up and held and remained so when set back down, and then ate squeeze up treats. He's a good boy who might have a slight tendency to overstimulate.

Thor tolerates attention and petting but may overstimulate and has a history of biting and swatting during interactions in the shelter. We recommend that he go to a home with some cat experience preferred and be well counseled in overstimulation, petting induced aggression, nervous cat behavior and or a tendency to become ramped up.

A volunteer writes: Thor deserves well his name. He is a handsome, elegant and smartly dressed gent, may be a little timid but very sweet and appreciative of petting and sweet words. Thor came to us without any other information than having some urinary troubles for possibly a few months. He seems to have been well cared for by his former family who could not afford his veterinary care. Thor is now much better and on a special diet to prevent the formation of stones in his urine. He is a sweet and good looking middle aged gentleman, a bit shy but who after some "pep talks" leans into pets, purrs and even starts playing with feather wands. He is well mannered and performed very well on his behavior evaluation. Thor would love to be a beloved pet once again and may be it could be with you!

UPDATE:Thor has been with us for over a month now. His patience, his exemplary behavior and sweetness have no boundaries. A cat like him so deserves a loving home. Spending time with him feels good. He is always available, kind and well mannered. Yes, there is soo much competition:the kittens, the younger cats and those who are not on a special diet. Thor has lots against him but he is a very sweet cat who will give a lot of love, comfort and loyalty to his new family. Will you consider Thor for your new forever best friend?

Upon being evaluated again, Tiffany appears to be displaying behaviors that indicate a very high level of FAS and quickly escalates to defensive aggression. She is noted to be a somewhat fearful cat in her previous home and takes some time to warm up to strangers and appreciates her boundaries being respected - making a shelter environment one that would be difficult for her to adjust to. While she may have some potential with socialization to be approached and adjust to the shelter, at this time, she displays behaviors that are not appropriate for general adoption or the adoptions floor. She displays high levels of FAS and during her assessment, and quickly escalated to defensive behaviors. The behavior team feels that she would do best in an adult-only home with experienced adopters that are willing to give her plenty of time to adjust to her new environment, and understand how to work with fearful cats. Her behaviors are likely shelter specific and the behavior team feels that once given time to decompress outside of the shelter, approached slowly and with respect for her boundaries, she will likely return to her previous playful, lap cat, and cuddly behaviors once she is comfortable with her new family and feels safe in her new home.

A volunteer writes: Seniors Toast and Avocado were discarded in a carrier among piles of trash waiting to be picked up by the sanitary truck. Luckily, an astute and concerned citizen spotted them and brought them to the Manhattan Care Center. Toast is a ten year old gentleman, a tabby who likely and understandably can not fathom "what just hit him"... He had a cold to make things even harder. How is a former pet supposed to handle himself in the face of such an unexpected and frightening hardship? Toast was a little cranky and fearful when his behavior was tested but, a few days down the line, he welcomed petting, even head bunted my hand with his neck and purred(see his video). I did not hear a hiss, I did not see a swat, just some reservation, some shyness.  Toast needs better than a cage. True, nothing is known about him(except that he lived with a thirteen year old dame, Avocado). Is he a good guy/or not. I would go for the latter... Feeling safe and loved (in a quiet and experienced home) is what will bring warmth and life to this abandoned elderly pet. We hope that Toast will pull at your heart strings and be your forever thankful four-legged companion!

Toose is a sweet and sensitive pup who is looking for a patient family that will help him feel safe and comfortable in his new home. After being surrendered when his owners could no longer care for him, Toose is ready for a fresh start with someone who understands that the best relationships are built with trust and time. While he may be a little shy at first, this gentle guy has so much potential to blossom once he knows he is safe.

My Ideal Home
Toose would thrive in a calm, predictable home with adopters who are willing to let him settle in at his own pace. He prefers to make new friends on his own terms and will appreciate a family who understands canine body language and respects his boundaries. With patience, positive reinforcement, and plenty of encouragement, Toose can continue gaining confidence and learning that the world is a safe place.

Good with Other Pets?
Toose's previous owners reported that he ignores other dogs while on walks. His history with dogs in a home environment is unknown, and during shelter interactions he appeared unsure around unfamiliar dogs. Slow, thoughtful introductions would be recommended to help him feel comfortable and successful around new canine friends.

Good with Kids?
Due to Toose's fearful nature and his preference for approaching new people at his own pace, a home with adults only is recommended. He would do best with people who can give him the time, space, and gentle guidance he needs to feel secure.

Things to Know
Toose is a quiet, gentle dog who enjoys taking things slowly. He walks nicely on leash and is happy to explore his surroundings at his own pace. His previous family shared that he can become mouthy during play, so continued practice with appropriate play skills and redirection to toys will help him succeed. Toose may bark or growl when unfamiliar people enter his home, but once he has time to warm up, he can become a friendly and loving companion. This sensitive sweetheart is looking for someone who will give him the patience and understanding he deserves. He considered me as I admired his big gorgeous face and brightly curious eyes. Uno came to us from a home with many other cats and we don't know much about his life before, but he's so sweetly interested in shelter life and carefully thinking about what he can do to join in. This, of course, is much easier said than done, but he samples the treats, plays with the toys we leave him, and waits right at the front for a chance to make the kind of entrance and introduction befitting a forever family. He's done his time on the NYC streets serving his community and keeping the peace. Oh the stories he could tell! And now he's looking for a retirement home where he can let his guard down and enjoy some comfort and TLC in his golden years. Ushi got this far in life by watching his back and keeping to himself. His heroes are those hardboiled movie detectives, keeping their collar up and their hat brim down, sniffing out corruption in the shadows and searching for truth in the seedy city. And old habits die hard, so at first Ushi seems aloof and withdrawn. But there's a real softie inside his stoic exterior. Once Ushi is feeling safe and happy he will literally melt into pets and cuddles. It's very rewarding to watch this big guy learn to trust humans and accept the delights of apartment living. "Oh, this soft comfy bed is for *me*? Don't mind if I do...!" Ushi is a creature of habit and routine. He'll stake out one or two favourite tucked-away nap spots that he'll return to day in, day out. And he takes mealtimes very seriously - he'll quietly sit by his food bowl until you get the message...! While he will sometimes scamper away to stay out of trouble, he's wise enough to know never to pick a fight - he is not aggressive. Ushi will be happiest in a quiet, chill, low-traffic home where the humans will respect his need for alone time - but also lavish him with the care and affection he deserves in the golden years of his remarkable, colorful life. My foster writes: Ushi is a shy cat who needs a little time to feel safe in a new home. At first he may keep some distance, but with patience and quiet companionship he slowly starts coming closer on his own. He has a few small imperfections. One ear looks a bit different, there are some spots on his legs without much fur, and sometimes he gets a little eye discharge. He loves canned food and squeeze treats. They make it much easier to win his trust. He also has some very funny habits. If you pet his lower back his butt pops right up, and if you touch his cheeks he immediately flops onto the floor and melts there to enjoy the attention. Ushi just needs someone patient and gentle. Once he feels comfortable, he becomes a very sweet and quietly affectionate companion. A volunteer writes: We're so glad Ushi is currently warm and safe at the Care Center, and we think he seems pretty pleased as well! Ever since he's come through our doors he's been sweet, calm, curious, and easy to handle, enjoying petting sessions and scarfing down lots of treats. He can sometimes be shy as he sizes up new human faces, but after a quick warm-up he's ready to make friends and enjoy the affection and interaction. Our behavior team can vouch for his comfort with people and generally chill demeanor, deeming Ushi to be a good fit for almost all types of households. We don't know what kind of life he had before he came to us, but it's a good bet that this wonderful guy was well socialized with people in a home. Now, he's ready to make the move to yours. Another volunteer writes: Ushi(Little Bear in German) was brought to us by the Good Samaritan who was taking care of him for years as an outdoor cat. He had a cold(now resolved)and was quite underweight and being a senior, it was about time for Ushi to find a safe haven for his golden years. Ushi likes to shelter in his cubby but say his name, bring some tasty treats and he will be out in nano seconds.. Ushi is a bit handshy but being a smart kitty, he is slowly easing himself into being an indoor pet. Ushi so deserves a new page in his life, filled with warmth, safety and love. What my friends at ACC say about me:

Uzi is a big "galoot" of a cat! He was at the front, sweet, friendly, and curious, loving treats and leaning in nicely for cheek rubs. He warmed up quickly, leaning in more with a high tail and enjoying all petting. He was curious and interested in possibly coming out of the kennel, and when picked up and held, he remained calm in the assessor's arms. When set back down, he remained at the front, pushing against the assessor's hand as if wanting either more attention or out of the kennel, or both.

Due to prior owner history (see separate notes) and a bite/scratch history we feel that this cat will do best in an experienced cat parent home.

A volunteer writes: Uzi was sleeping so soundly that it was momentarily difficult for me to imagine that he's ever had a care in the world, but then I noticed the note explaining that his blanket and toys help to provide some of the security he's been looking for. Years","type":"Dog","species":"Dog","link":"https://nycacc.app/browse/248787","gender":"Male","summaryHtml":"Meet Will!
Will is a long-stay resident who arrived through NYPD after his owner experienced housing insecurity, and he's been waiting patiently for his chance at a fresh start. He's an energetic, social boy with a big personality who's ready for someone who can help channel all that enthusiasm into positive outlets.

My Ideal Home
Will would do best in an active home that can keep up with his energy and help him continue building impulse control through structure and enrichment. He thrives with mental stimulation like food puzzles, long-lasting chews, sniff games, and consistent daily exercise. He'll shine with a patient adopter who enjoys training and can help him turn his excitement into good manners.

Good with Other Pets?
Will should be the only pet in the home. He has shown strong interest in small animals at the shelter and has a reported history of conflict with other dogs, so a dog-free home is recommended.

Good with Kids?
Due to his exuberance and tendency to jump up, ACC recommends a home without very young children. He may be open to older, dog-savvy kids with proper introductions.

Things to Know
Will is a bright, affectionate dog who sometimes struggles with impulse control when he's excited. He may jump up, counter-surf, or become overly focused on food, but he is also responsive to handlers and enjoys engagement and training. On leash, he can pull moderately and occasionally fixate on treats, so continued practice with leash manners and structure will help him succeed. With consistency, enrichment, and positive reinforcement, Will has so much potential to thrive in a home environment.

Woody arrived at our care center as a stray, and his history is mostly a mystery. He's a very sweet, playful, and energetic dog who enjoys bouncing around and interacting with people he trusts. Woody loves interactive play, especially chasing and retrieving toys. He appreciates slow introductions to new people and places and prefers to approach on his own terms for pets and attention.

My Ideal Home
Woody would do best in a calm, adult-only household where he can set the pace for interactions. He benefits from consistent routines, gentle guidance, and positive reinforcement. Woody needs adopters who are patient and experienced with dogs that have touch sensitivities and mild resource guarding. A home that can provide cooperative handling and safe enrichment will help him thrive.

Good with Kids?
No - Woody is recommended for homes without children under 13. He prefers calm interactions and can become stressed in high-energy environments.

Good with Other Pets?
Woody has limited dog-to-dog experience. When properly introduced, he can be playful and gentle, but he may be pushy around treats. He is not recommended for homes with cats or smaller pets due to his size and energy.

Leash Manners
Woody walks well on leash with experienced handlers. He can be excitable when first leaving his kennel but quickly focuses on exploring once outside. Pulling is minimal with calm, consistent leadership.

Behavior Determination
Level 3 / Experienced Adopters - Woody requires a knowledgeable and patient home due to his touch sensitivities, mild resource guarding, and medical considerations. He responds best to calm, predictable, and positive interactions.

Other Fun Facts
Woody has a joyful, bouncy personality and loves games of chase and fetch. He enjoys bonding with people who respect his boundaries and allows him to approach for attention. While he likes to assert independence, he is very affectionate with those he trusts and thrives in a patient, structured environment.

More like jiggling by my side than walking, really, as his whole jello body quakes with joy with each step. I adore his cartoon face, the way his teefies sometimes get stuck in his lips and his freakishly large milk chocolate eyes. He loves to play with toys, loves attention and loves to be out of his kennel. A volunteer writes: Yosemite was found sitting frozen on a blanket with other cats in the park. Too scared to move or enjoy the food that had been left out for them, it seems like this group was all just hoping for the best but expecting much less. Fortunately for Yosemite and company, things started moving in the right direction when someone scooped them up and brought them to us. It's unlikely Yosemite interpreted this as a best case scenario because the shelter really does have quite a lot going on, maybe even too much for a quiet guy like Yosemite, but we've been working to convince him that sometimes the best comes in steps and even baby steps at that. Crouching in the back of his cubby, he didn't seem very interested in the toys, treats, or pets I had to offer, but I have to believe that Yosemite is only waiting for his chance.

Another volunteer writes: Yosemite more recently decided to come out of his shell. He is sits more and more on his balcony or rests in his "living room". He is definitively interested in seeing people but has still a very hard time to trust us, even those he has seen the faces again and again. Yosemite likes to play though as you can see on his photos. He enjoys catnip toys and feather wands. He occasionally will accept a brief pet on his head when he samples treats. My adoption fee has been sponsored by a generous donor! Zuessey is a 7-year-old boy who came to us as an owner surrender when his family could no longer care for him. He's a sweet, social guy who is now looking for a steady, understanding home where he can feel secure and supported as he settles into a new routine.

Personality
Zuessey is an affectionate, people focused dog who enjoys being near his handlers and staying involved in whatever is going on. He is social in the room, often staying close, exploring calmly, and coming over readily for attention and treats. Once comfortable, he shows a friendly, engaged side and enjoys interaction with people.

He can be a bit mouthy when taking treats and may become anxious at times, especially in situations that are unfamiliar or when left alone, so he benefits from structure and reassurance in his environment.

Leash Walks
Zuessey walks with mild pulling on leash and generally stays manageable with guidance. He is not reactive to people and tends to focus more on moving forward with his handler than on distractions.

Social Behavior
Zuessey is friendly and comfortable with handling, accepting pets and treats with a neutral, easygoing posture. He tends to stay near people and checks in frequently, showing a desire for connection and reassurance.

With other dogs, he has shown interest and playful behaviors, but interactions can become overexcited, so structured introductions and supervision are important.

Home Life
Zuessey has some anxiety when left alone and may benefit from a consistent routine and gradual alone-time training. He does best in a home that can provide patience, structure, and positive outlets for his energy and stress.

Fun Fact
Zuessey is the kind of dog who wants to be part of everything. If you're there, he's there too, quietly keeping you company and waiting for the next treat or moment of attention.
